Counteract the Virginia Tech pass rush with quick-hitting throws, keep the defense on its heels, and, on the other side, get the defense off the field. Virginia Tech isn't always great on third downs, and SMU is third in the nation, with offenses converting just 27% of their chances. Virginia Tech vs SMU Prediction, Betting Lines SMU is a much different team in Gerald J. Ford. The offense is good no matter where it plays, but this year, the defense steps its game up several notches, especially against the run. The three worst games on the season for the run defense were all on the road, and the Hokies won't grind it out enough. Virginia Tech is 2-2 when it doesn't get to 130 yards on the ground. SMU hasn't allowed more than 125 this year at home. picks.blurb: 2026 Week 10 Preview: Virginia Tech Hokies @ SMU Mustangs | Underdog Dynasty Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Rest of the FBS Community Underdog Dynasty November 5, 2026 Underdog Dynasty Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Conference USA Sun Belt Conference American Athletic Conference Betting FanDuel College Football Odds College Football Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Conference USA Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications ACC Rhett Lashlee and James Franklin meet again, this time, in a de facto ACC title elimination game. Time and date: Friday, November 6 at 7:00 p.m. ET Network: ESPN Location: Gerald J. Ford Stadium — Dallas, TX Spread: SMU (-6) Over/under: 56.5 All-time series: SMU leads, 2-1 Last meeting: SMU 28, Virginia Tech 25 — September 21, 1974 Current streak: SMU, 2 (1973-74) Setting the scene While No. 1 Miami (FL) and No. 14 Wake Forest are the only ACC teams that reside in the AP Top 25, the conference title race is far from finished. There are five two-loss teams lurking right behind, and two of them clash Friday night in Dallas. It’s the first meeting between SMU and Virginia Tech as ACC opponents, however, it’s a familiar head coaching matchup: Rhett Lashlee and James Franklin stood on opposite sidelines as recently as 2024 in the College Football Playoff. There’s plenty on the line for the bowl eligible opponents. A win would do wonders for remaining in the ACC race, especially for SMU, which can still capture a tiebreaker against Wake Forest. But a third conference loss is essentially an elimination in a 17-team league. Virginia Tech Hokies outlook Virginia Tech (6-2, 3-2 ACC) can make another statement on the road after its bye week. The Hokies haven’t rattled off seven wins in a regular season since 2019, but that streak could end Friday in year one of the James Franklin era. Virginia Tech is fresh off its biggest win under Franklin, taking down Clemson 20-16 in Death Valley on Oct. 24. Close games have been commonplace for the Hokies this season. Each of their last six contests were decided by 10 points or fewer. Three featured lead changes in the final five minutes, while another ended on a missed field goal attempt that would have resulted in a lead change. The restoration of Virginia Tech football can be attributed to the passing game. Quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer followed Franklin from Penn State and has drastically improved in his junior campaign. Grunkemeyer has connected on an efficient 71.4 percent of attempts — seventh nationally among quarterbacks with 100 attempts — and has delivered 17 touchdowns against two interceptions. Grunkemeyer has eclipsed 300 yards three times and finished seven of his eight starts without throwing a pick. Two receivers have carried a bulk of the load. Wide receiver Que’Sean Brown ranks atop the team with 51 receptions and 685 receiving yards, and he’s secured at least five receptions in all eight games. Tight end Luke Reynolds has also been a matchup nightmare for defenses. Reynolds’ 50 receptions rank first and his 491 receiving yards ranks third among all FBS tight ends. While a bulk of his production occurred in September, his outing against Clemson was a productive one, snagging two touchdowns on seven receptions. The Hokies aren’t as adept in the run game, where they check in at 111th in the FBS with 3.7 yards per carry. They don’t incorporate much quarterbaack mobility and primarily rely on the duo of Jeffrey Overton Jr. and Marcellous Hawkins Jr. Overton, a common weapon in the receiving game, showed the extent of his powers in a 209-yard rushing explosion against Boston College. Hawkins has been a steady secondary back, and he’s tied for the team lead with five rushing touchdowns. Virginia Tech only surrendered more than 26 points once this season, and that was a Friday night matchup against Pittsburgh. The Hokies’ defense has been a positive for the team, tied for 35th in points allowed and ranked 27th in yards allowed per game. Their strength involves limiting the run, where they give up just 93.4 yards per game on a 3.0 average. Sacks heavily factor into that total, and Virginia Tech is the best in the ACC and the sixth-best in the nation at getting to the quarterback, producing 3.4 sacks per game. It’s a defensive end led effort. Aycen Stevens ranks first in the conference with 8.0 sacks, while his fellow defensive ends Cortez Harris and Mylachi Williams have 5.0 and 4.5, respectively. The Hokies haven’t been as strong on the back end, but they prevent explosive plays well. No team has recorded a 50-yard completion on this defense all season. But what Virginia Tech needs to improve upon is its turnover output. The Hokies forced just five takeaways through eight games, causing the team to enter Friday with a minus-4 in the turnover battle this season. SMU Mustangs outlook SMU (6-2, 4-2 ACC) dropped from the rankings after a heartbreaking 30-27 loss at Syracuse last weekend. It was only the Mustangs’ fourth conference defeat since joining the ACC, and the third in which they held a lead in the final minute. However, SMU has never lost back-to-back ACC games and owns an 11-0 record in ACC play at home, giving Rhett Lashlee’s team the perfect opportunity to bounce back and remain in the conference title race. Slow starts have been the Mustangs’ kryptonite. In their last five ACC games, they haven’t scored more than 13 points in a half or entered the break with a lead larger than three. However, they’ve won each of their last five second halves, finishing a plus-68 over that span. SMU’s offense is led by Kevin Jennings, who is one of seven passers averaging over 300 yards per game. This season has been a masterclass in efficiency for the senior, who is completing passes at a 73.7 percent clip — the third-highest rate in the country among quarterbacks with 100 attempts. Jennings has also thrown 152 consecutive passes without an interception, with his last misfire coming in the first quarter of a Sept. 26 matchup against Missouri State. The Mustangs’ receiver room is as deep as they come, with five different players over the 200-yard threshold. Yamir Knight is the leader with 44 receptions for 523 yards, while Yannick Smith, Jalen Cooper, and Jalen Hale can also pose as explosive threats for an offense that ranks fifth nationally in 50+ yard receptions. Tight ends Randy Pittman Jr. and Theo Melin Öhrstrom are also incorporated into the passing game, and they tie for the team lead with four receptions apiece. Unlike SMU’s first ACC defeat at Louisville, last Saturday’s loss to Syracuse was largely determined in the trenches. The Mustangs uncharacteristically allowed six sacks, accounting for 43 percent of their season total. Additionally, they struggled to create space for the running backs, which never broke off an explosive gain. Kendrick Raphael has posted three 100-yard games already in ACC play, and he can also do damage out of the backfield as a receiving option. SMU’s defense didn’t necessarily have a bad outing at Syracuse, limiting the Orange to 5.9 yards per passing attempt and 3.7 yards per rush. But the Mustangs surrendered conversions on all four of Syracuse’s fourth down attempts, allowing the Orange to sustain otherwise lost drives. A veteran defensive line full of super seniors is the strength of the unit. SMU ranks 15th nationally with 2.9 sacks per game, and eighth-year senior Marques White leads the way with 5.5 sacks, while the rest of the sacks are quite evenly distributed. The pressure goes hand-in-hand with a strong passing defense, and SMU ranks 28th nationally in fewest passing yards allowed at 182 per game. That is the most improved element of the Mustangs from last year, but losing starting strong safety Tyren Polley for the year could make things difficult down the road. Sael Reyes stepped up last game with 10 tackles in his second start of the season, while Jimmy Wyrick recorded eight from the other safety spot. Lastly, turnovers have been a significant determinant in SMU results this season. The Mustangs lost the turnover battle 5-0 in their two losses, and they’re the only bowl eligible team at a minus-5 or worse this season. These 6-2 teams are structured somewhat similarly: strong passing attacks with tight end utilization, dominant defensive fronts that repeatedly get to the quarterback, and solid defenses hampered by poor turnover margins. Short weeks oftentimes favor the home team, and SMU remains perfect against ACC opponents at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. Given SMU’s discrepancy between first and second half performance, Virginia Tech may enter halftime with the lead, but the Mustangs ultimately rally behind Kevin Jennings in the fourth quarter to secure a one-score win on The Hilltop. One of the most underrated rivalries in college football history is back in Week 10, with Utah hosting BYU at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City at noon ET on Saturday, Nov. 7. The BYU vs. Utah rivalry , aka the Holy War, will feature a new head coach for the first time in a decade as Morgan Scalley leads the Utes as 2.5-point favorites in a ranked showdown between these two programs. However, Scalley is familiar with this rivalry, having coached and played in it, but can he end Utah's losing streak, or will BYU's recent dominance make the Cougars the popular pick among college football analysts? BYU vs Utah 2026 preview Kalani Sitake (91-46) Head coach (record with school) Morgan Scalley (8-0) SP+ special teams BYU vs Utah odds BYU vs Utah prediction In the first Holy War matchup ever where both programs are ranked in the top 10, Utah is in a perfect position to end its losing streak and beat BYU for the first time since 2019. There's a chance BYU star running back LJ Martin will be back for this game (he hasn't played since Oct. 3), but even if he is, Utah's defense is equipped to slow him down. And if he's not back, the Cougars could be in trouble if they're once again putting everything on Bear Bachmeier's shoulders. This Utah defense has one of the best secondaries in the country, and if Bachmeier alone has to carry the running game, BYU will struggle to generate enough points to keep this close. The Utes' defense ranks No. 13 in points allowed per opportunity (2.70), No. 19 in success rate (39.4%), and No. 20 in third- and fourth-down success rate (37.7%). This is also a bad matchup for BYU's defense, with Utah having one of the best run games in the country (19th in EPA per rush), and BYU struggling to stop the run, ranking 74th in rush success rate on defense (45%). If Devon Dampier , Wayshawn Parker , and Utah's offensive line go to work on the ground and find early success, BYU could be in for a long afternoon in Salt Lake City. Score prediction: Utah 29, BYU 23 Who are the stars of BYU vs Utah 2026? Bear Bachmeier, QB, BYU The story of Bear Bachmeier is slowly becoming a legend in Provo. He was supposed to play at Stanford, and even enrolled there last year as a freshman, but hit the transfer portal during spring practices. Bachmeier decided to team up with his brother, Tiger, at BYU and won the starting QB job as a true freshman. After leading the team to a 12-2 record and taking home Big 12 Offensive Freshman of the Year last season, Bachmeier has been even better as a sophomore and ranks top 20 nationally in QBR (79). Built like a linebacker and wearing No. 47, Bachmeier is as unconventional a QB as it gets, but he already upset Notre Dame earlier this season, and he'll be the key to another BYU win in the Holy War. Devon Dampier, QB, Utah One of the most dynamic QBs in the country since his days at New Mexico , Devon Dampier already has 7,000+ passing yards, 2,500+ rushing yards, and nearly 100 total touchdowns in his career. After two seasons with the Lobos, one in which he ran for 19 touchdowns, Dampier ended up following his offensive coordinator at New Mexico, Jason Beck, to Utah last season, and he hit the ground running by winning Big 12 Offensive Newcomer of the Year. When Kyle Whittingham took Beck with him to Michigan, Dampier stayed and has been a maestro in new offensive coordinator Kevin McGiven's offense. Dampier already had 23 total touchdowns this year, and his mobility will be the X-factor for Utah against BYU, like it was against Houston. LJ Martin, RB, BYU It's not clear yet whether LJ Martin will play in the Holy War this year after suffering an ankle injury on Oct. 3, but it's been reported that he could make his return against Utah. The Cougars could certainly use him after he was their engine last season when he won Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year after totaling more than 1,500 yards from scrimmage. A future NFL pick, Martin is one of the best bruising backs in the country and was top 10 nationally in rushing yards after contact in 2025 (893). Zereou Williams, OT, Utah Somehow, Utah has another potential first-round pick at offensive tackle. Last year's duo of Spencer Fano and Caleb Lomu was the best in college football, and both were selected on the first night of the 2026 NFL Draft, and it turns out their backup might be just as good. Zereou "Big Z" Williams was a late-bloomer who focused on basketball before picking football back up again as a senior in high school. He bided his time at Utah as a backup and played just 265 snaps from 2021 to 2025. As a first-year starter this season, he's been playing at an All-American level, allowing zero sacks and just six pressures while paving the way for one of college football's best run games. He'll need to set the tone for Utah's offense in the Holy War. Cade Uluave, LB, BYU One of college football's best hidden gems for the last few seasons at Cal , where he won Pac-12 Freshman of the Year in 2023 and earned first-team All-ACC honors last season, Cade Uluave has been a perfect fit at BYU. With a non-stop motor and a penchant for violent hits, Uluave has been a weapon for the Cougars this season with 52 tackles, 19 defensive stops, 16 pressures, and 4.5 TFLs. He'll need to be an enforcer against Utah's run game if BYU is going to pull off the upset and win a fourth straight Holy War. Rabbit Evans, SAF, Utah Utah has one of the most underrated secondaries in the country, but the rise of Rabbit Evans has been meteoric. Evans began his college career playing JUCO ball at Blinn for two years and earning NCJCA All-American honors. After being a backup for most of 2024 at Utah, Evans missed most of 2025 with an injury. But he's come back with a vengeance this season and has been a ball magnet for the Utes, with two interceptions and two fumble recoveries. More importantly, he's been a dynamo in coverage, allowing just a 16.1 NFL QB rating. Bachmeier is going to need to know where he is on every play. BYU vs Utah rivalry history: Holy War 9 (1979-1987) Longest win streak 9 (1929-1937) Largest margin of victory 649-449-28 (.589) Program record 758-494-32 (.603) Claimed national titles (recognized) Conference championships Heisman winners Consensus All-Americans Weeks in the AP Poll Weeks at No. 1 Bowl games (record) NFL draft picks First-round picks There's some controversy around when the Holy War began; BYU says the first game wasn't played until 1922, but if you ask Utah , the rivalry began in 1896. Either way, this rivalry is one of the most interesting in college football because of the runs of dominance, the hatred, the legendary coaches, and the religious wrinkle, hence the nickname. According to Utah, the first Holy War was played on April 6, 1896, which the Utes won 12-4 in Salt Lake City. They then won again later that year, 6-0, when the two met again on Nov. 14, 1896.

No. 8 BYU, after a week of remedial tackle drills after losing to UCF, will host a struggling Arizona State squad on Saturday. Utah's long road test could be a thing. But it won't. BYU will improve its tackling because it must. This is the setting for the Big 12's two top-10-ranked teams from the state of Utah as the conference race tightens down the stretch, determining who will earn tickets to the league title game in Arlington. BYU defensive coordinator Kelly Poppinga told reporters this week that missed tackles led to BYU's first loss of the season at UCF, but he wasn't going to overreact. "I'm never a guy that overreacts that way. I think just stay the course. You trust the process. "We did our tackling drill yesterday, and we did our tackling drill today, and every other coach has done their stuff in their position drills. "And so, I'm not going to sit here and overreact. I just think it's something we've got to continue to get better at," he continued. "And I think every team in college football goes through just being able to go through the techniques and fundamentals and not lose that as the season goes on, but get better at everything every day." Poppinga said BYU has yet to play its best full game of the season, although the Notre Dame game came close. But even that night, some things could have been improved. "We have great leadership, great experience and guys who have played a lot of football," he said. "Kalani (Sitake) wants us to play a full 60 minutes — I think we came close to that in the Iowa State game and there were glimpses in the Notre Dame game and throughout the whole entire season." In Cincinnati, the Ute defense will have its hands full with Bearcat running back Tabb Cole, and he'll be running behind a talented offensive line that will challenge Utah defenders. At the same time, Cincy's defense will have a huge challenge in slowing down Wayshawn Parker and Ute quarterback Davon Dampier. Cincinnati head coach Scott Satterfield described Utah's offense as "extremely talented" and noted that they stretch the defense horizontally from sideline to sideline, creating thin areas. "They can push the ball down the field in the passing game and 'just stay on track' without many negative plays, keeping down-and-distance manageable," said Satterfield. The problem for Cincinnati, a place where there was a storming of the field last week after the victory over Texas Tech, is that the Bearcat defense is horrible, among the nation's worst when it comes to stopping good offenses. That's now a recipe for dealing with Kevin McGiven's offense at home or on the road. Can't bring a cap gun to a real battle, but that's all Cincinnati's defense has to point at Utah's offensive churn. No. 7 BYU visits No. 3 Utah on Saturday, November 7, in the first Holy War where both teams are ranked in the top 10. The 10 a.m. local kickoff at Rice-Eccles Stadium adds another wrinkle. Utah is 8–0 and sits atop the Big 12 at 5–0. BYU is 7–1 and shares second place with Texas Tech, but its loss to UCF leaves little room for error. Utah opened as roughly a 5.5-point favorite with a total of 48.5. These predictions go against the safe script, a ground-game surprise, a Utah quarterback performance and a late BYU rally that falls short. Let's take a look at the bold predictions for this marquee matchup. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) LJ Martin plays, but Bear Bachmeier is the star Rob Gray-Imagn Images LJ Martin will return and play a limited role, yet Bachmeier will be the one who carries BYU's offense. Martin has missed four games with a leg injury and has not played since the October 3 win over TCU. He is still BYU's leading rusher at 344 yards and 7.8 yards per carry, so the Cougars badly need him. But offensive coordinator Aaron Roderick said Martin is "not all the way back yet," which suggests a managed workload. The prediction is Bachmeier throws for 275 yards and rushes for two touchdowns, outproducing Martin in every category. Bachmeier has already accounted for most of BYU's rushing output without Martin, with 336 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns on 80 carries. He also has 1,750 passing yards and 12 touchdowns. Utah's secondary is among the best in the country, so BYU may need Martin's presence as a decoy more than as a workhorse. That could open play-action and RPO looks for Bachmeier. Devon Dampier and Wayshawn Parker combine for 300 total yards Utah's offense will hinge on its quarterback and running back, and together they will account for 300 total yards and four touchdowns. Dampier has been outstanding, with 12 total touchdowns against one interception over his last four games. He has completed 69.6 percent of his passes for 1,876 yards and 18 touchdowns this season. Parker is the other half. He has 726 rushing yards and nine touchdowns, and Utah's ground game ranks eighth nationally at 226.9 yards per game. BYU's rush defense is strong in raw yardage, ranking 20th at 100 yards per game, but Covers notes it ranks only 74th in rush success rate. That gap suggests Utah can win with misdirection and efficiency instead of pure power. The Utes also rank third nationally in third-down efficiency at 54.1 percent, which helps them sustain drives against an aggressive linebacker group. Utah will lose right tackle Kelvin Obot for the season, but the line has still been one of the best in the country. I expect the Utes to handle his absence. Utah wins 31–27 and snaps BYU's three-game streak The final prediction is a four-point Utah win that comes down to the last possession. BYU has won three straight in the series, while Utah had won nine in a row before that. Utah has still won 14 straight overall, the longest active streak in the FBS. Utah's offense should control the game early, but BYU will keep it close by converting in the red zone. A late Cougars touchdown will make it a one-possession game before the Utes' defense finishes with a stop. The projected 58 total points would clear the 48.5-point line comfortably. The point spread would also come down to a single score, giving BYU a cover as a 5.5-point underdog. The result would leave Utah in prime position for a Big 12 title game berth and a playoff bid. BYU would stay alive in the conference race, but it would have almost no margin left. No. 9 BYU @ No. 3 Utah This Holy War might be the holiest of them all: Utah hosting bitter rival BYU, with the winner in the driver's seat for a Playoff spot. It’s the first time both teams have been ranked in the top 10 for this matchup, and I can’t wait to start the day with this one. I think BYU might win outright. It has been tested with its win over Notre Dame just a few weeks ago. Yes, it lost to UCF the following week in a typical trap game — big home win followed by a road conference game. Otherwise, the Cougars have handled business, even though the scores don’t seem that impressive. BYU is built on defense. It is 13th in yards per play and it limits explosives. It does not rush the passer all that well, but against Utah’s rushing attack, that might not be needed. BYU’s defense already faced a high-powered offense in the Irish and limited it to a negative EPA rushing day. Utah’s offensive production slowly ticked down when conference play started, but it did bounce back last week against a poor Cincinnati defense. Utah has played one defense in the same realm as BYU and that was Houston. Utah struggled to score, only putting up 21 points with seven of those happening super late after forcing a Houston turnover. Will the BYU offense find a groove against Utah? (Getty Images) It’s fair to also believe BYU’s offense might struggle in this game. However, it appears the Cougars are getting stud running back LJ Martin back, and they are much better when Martin is on the field. He’s averaging almost eight yards a carry with 20% of his rushes going for 10+ yards. Utah’s defense is the typical physical front against the run, but BYU is the best offense the Utes have faced all season. Utah’s pass rush concerns me. It is 80th in pressure rate and unless it blitzes, it isn't able to get to the quarterback. Seems less than ideal against BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier. I see these teams as even. They are both defensively based with an offense that wants to run the ball. That’s too many points in a game like this. I’ll take BYU to cover. Schwartz's Pick: BYU -4.5 No. 5 Alabama @ No. 14 LSU In the newly-released CFP rankings, Alabama is fifth and is an underdog at LSU by almost a touchdown. I do lean towards LSU at -6, but that number feels big. Instead, I’m going to fade Alabama’s offense in this game. Alabama is facing its fourth straight difficult defense, and in the first three games, we’ve seen the offensive efficiency drop. Quarterback Keelon Russell is nearing the end of his first season as a starting quarterback, and he’s been mostly excellent for his age. However, he has struggled the last three weeks outside the end of the Texas A&M game. Against Georgia, Tennessee and A&M, he completed only 60% of passes with just four passing touchdowns and three interceptions. Alabama’s beat-up offensive line has allowed 11 sacks in the three previous games. Now, the Tide play an LSU defense that’s first in sacks per pressure and 11th in pressure rate. The Bama offensive line and Russell were noticeably affected by the environment in Tennessee, and now they are at LSU. I feel most comfortable with Alabama not scoring much in this game. away.headline: BYU releases initial LJ Martin injury status ahead of Utah game
away.blurb: On Wednesday night, the BYU football program provided the first official injury update for LJ Martin ahead of a top 10 matchup with Utah. Martin is "doubtful" for the game against the Utes. The "doubtful" designation is reserved for the players that have a 25% chance to play. However, just a few minutes before the injury report came out, ESPN's Pete Thamel reported that Martin is considered "questionable" for this weekend. The "questionable" designation is reserved for players with a 50% chance to play. Thamel reported that if Martin returns, "he's not expected to be 100% and could be limited." Thamel added more information, saying "[Martin is] trending to dress, be available, and have some impact on the game. A final decision will be made later this week." Martin was back practicing on Tuesday, according to Aaron Roderick. The last time he played was in early October against TCU. If Martin can't go, BYU will turn to Preston Rex who was not available for the ASU game. Rex had a breakout game against Notre Dame before suffering an injury against UCF. If Saleapaga isn't available, expect more sets with three wide receivers. That would leave Walker Lyons on the field for most of the game. If Evan Johnson can't play, BYU will turn to Jayven Williams and Therrian Alexander III at cornerback. Williams and Alexander shut down two of the best wide receivers in the Big 12 last week. They are more than capable of holding it down on the outside. The bigger question will be who BYU plays at nickel. The Cougars started Cannon DeVries at that spot to start the season, but DeVries has primarily been used for punt return duties since he suffered an injury. The ASU game was the first time DeVries had seen defensive snaps since suffering the injury. He played 14 snaps. LJ Martin and Evan Johnson Officially Ruled Out for BYU Against ASU If Martin returns, it would be the first time BYU has had its full compliment of running backs since the season opener. Other Injury Updates on BYU Starters BYU also provided injury updates on key starters Roger Saleapaga and Evan Johnson. Saleapaga left the game against ASU with an injury, and Johnson suffered what appeared to be a serious ankle injury against UCF. Johnson did not play against Arizona State last weekend. Most of the time, BYU had three safeties on the field. BYU averaged 2.7 safeties on the field at a time against ASU. True freshman Kennan Pula has seen his role grow over the last few weeks. home.headline: BYU releases initial LJ Martin injury status ahead of Utah game
home.blurb: On Wednesday night, the BYU football program provided the first official injury update for LJ Martin ahead of a top 10 matchup with Utah. Martin is "doubtful" for the game against the Utes. The "doubtful" designation is reserved for the players that have a 25% chance to play. However, just a few minutes before the injury report came out, ESPN's Pete Thamel reported that Martin is considered "questionable" for this weekend. The "questionable" designation is reserved for players with a 50% chance to play. Thamel reported that if Martin returns, "he's not expected to be 100% and could be limited." Thamel added more information, saying "[Martin is] trending to dress, be available, and have some impact on the game. A final decision will be made later this week." Martin was back practicing on Tuesday, according to Aaron Roderick. The last time he played was in early October against TCU. If Martin can't go, BYU will turn to Preston Rex who was not available for the ASU game. Rex had a breakout game against Notre Dame before suffering an injury against UCF. If Saleapaga isn't available, expect more sets with three wide receivers. That would leave Walker Lyons on the field for most of the game. If Evan Johnson can't play, BYU will turn to Jayven Williams and Therrian Alexander III at cornerback. Williams and Alexander shut down two of the best wide receivers in the Big 12 last week. They are more than capable of holding it down on the outside. The bigger question will be who BYU plays at nickel. The Cougars started Cannon DeVries at that spot to start the season, but DeVries has primarily been used for punt return duties since he suffered an injury. The ASU game was the first time DeVries had seen defensive snaps since suffering the injury. He played 14 snaps. LJ Martin and Evan Johnson Officially Ruled Out for BYU Against ASU If Martin returns, it would be the first time BYU has had its full compliment of running backs since the season opener. Other Injury Updates on BYU Starters BYU also provided injury updates on key starters Roger Saleapaga and Evan Johnson. Saleapaga left the game against ASU with an injury, and Johnson suffered what appeared to be a serious ankle injury against UCF. Johnson did not play against Arizona State last weekend. Most of the time, BYU had three safeties on the field. BYU averaged 2.7 safeties on the field at a time against ASU. True freshman Kennan Pula has seen his role grow over the last few weeks. He played 24 snaps against the Sun Devils. The Tigers (6-2, 3-2 SEC) have already blown out league foes Florida and Texas A&M at home this season and are 13-3 at Faurot Field against league opposition since 2023. Taking on Texas (6-2, 3-2) represents an uptick in competition, but the Tigers shouldn't be lacking confidence. Florida was No. 8 in the AP poll when it arrived at Mizzou on Oct. 3. It left with a 45-17 loss that legitimized Missouri and showed its full potential. Since then, we've also seen Missouri's floor, which was found in a 31-3 loss at Ole Miss on Oct. 17. But after a bye week and a 34-10 "get right" win over Arkansas in Week 9, the Tigers appear to be back on track. The Longhorns are entering off wins over Ole Miss and Mississippi State , but their vaunted offense is still falling short of expectations. Is this the point when everything will start to click for quarterback Arch Manning ? If a Texas team that spent four weeks at No. 1 earlier this season is going to meet expectations, a breakthrough needs to come soon. Texas vs. Missouri: Need to know Injuries mount for Texas: Injuries are adding up for the Longhorns, who enter this matchup with star receivers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman listed as questionable. Wingo is dealing with a quad injury while Coleman is working through a shoulder issue. Both have appeared in all eight games for Texas up to this point while combining to catch 11 of Arch Manning's 15 touchdown passes. Star edge rusher Collin Simmons is also questionable after missing Texas' past two games because of an ankle injury. That's a lot of star power in the "questionable" category for Texas. By contrast, Missouri's injury report is nearly clean. Welcome back, Ahmad: Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy made his 2026 debut last week, carrying the football twice in the Tigers' win over Arkansas. The 2025 All-American has been on the mend from a gunshot wound, and his return adds to a running back room that already features the SEC's leading rusher. Jamal Roberts became the conference's first back to surpass 1,000 yards for the season while rushing for 138 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries in a win over Arkansas. Roberts surpassed 200 yards in wins over Florida and Texas A&M last month. Gaining traction against Texas will be tough. No team has averaged more than four yards per rush attempt against Texas. College Football playoff implications: Texas' chance to reach the College Football Playoff will improve to 67.5% with a win, according to the CBS Sports CFB Forecaster. They will drop to 22.8% with a loss. If the Longhorns lose, they would need to win out against LSU, Arkansas and Texas A&M in order to potentially reach the 12-team field as a three-loss team. Missouri's chances to make the CFP will improve to 16.1% with a win. Those hopes would crater to 1.6% with a loss. The Tigers close with Georgia , Kentucky and Oklahoma . If Arch Manning can just take care of the football like he did last week, Texas can lean on its defense, win the field position battle and put stress on a Missouri defense that showed real vulnerability in losses to Mississippi State and Ole Miss. Former coach Gary Pinkel turned Missouri into a Big 12 contender in the 2000s, but the Tigers could never get over the hump against a Texas squad in the heart of its golden era under Mack Brown . They came closest in 2008, when Missouri quarterback Chase Daniel and Texas quarterback Colt McCoy combined for 655 yards passing. McCoy accounted for four total touchdowns for a Texas team that went 12-1 but missed out on a chance to play for a national championship after a wrenching last-second loss at Texas Tech in Week 9. Texas defensive lineman Maraad Watson (88) returns a fumble for a touchdown during the game against Mississippi State at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Know the foe: Missouri Last week: Beat Arkansas, 34-10 Players to watch: QB Austin Simmons , a 6-foot-4, 220-pound senior, once seemed like the heir apparent at Ole Miss but transferred to Missouri this past offseason after the emergence of current Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss. He's averaging 244 yards passing a game on 63.3% passing with 17 passing touchdowns compared to just two interceptions. RB Jamal Roberts , a 6-foot, 215-pound senior, stepped into a starring role after All-SEC running back Ahmad Hardy got shot in the leg at a concert in May and missed the first seven games of this season following surgery. Roberts leads the SEC with 1,005 yards rushing and averages 5.3 yards per carry. LB Nicholas Rodriguez, a 6-foot, 225-pound junior, leads the SEC with 11 tackles and game and forced a fumble in last week's win over Arkansas. His sideline-to-sideline range anchors the Tiger run defense. Central Texas connections: None. When Texas has the ball The Longhorns have issues running the ball, and Missouri prides itself on stopping the run. The ground game doesn't seem like a recipe for Longhorn success, especially since Texas running backs Hollywood Smothers and Derrek Cooper remain limited by injuries. Longhorn RB Raleek Brown followed up a 157-yard game against Ole Miss with just 30 yards rushing in last week's win over Mississippi State, and Missouri ranks third in SEC play by allowing only 104.8 yards rushing a game. Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) runs the ball during the game against Mississippi State at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Missouri ranks just 12 th in the SEC with 11 sacks in league play, but the Longhorns have struggled to protect QB Arch Manning while allowing 20 sacks in five SEC games. If a revamped Texas line with two tackles in new positions in right tackle Andre Cojoe and left tackle Melvin Siani can give Manning time, he may exploit a Tiger defense that gives up 260.4 yards passing a game in league play. When Missouri has the ball The Tigers like to pound the ball, especially since Hardy made his season debut last week against Arkansas. If Hardy can find the form that helped him rush for 3,000 yards and 29 TDs over his first two collegiate seasons, he'll team with Roberts in arguably the best backfield in college football. But Texas gives up yards on the ground grudgingly; the defense allows just 98.4 yards per game rushing in SEC play, which ranks only behind Georgia. The secondary may be the most beat-up unit on the squad, which is saying something for the bruised and battered Longhorns. Graceson Littleton , an elite slot corner, will likely miss the game. So could starting cornerback Kade Phillips. Texas could compensate by moving top corner Bo Mascoe to the slot, which is a critical position for the Longhorns' defense that ranks 10 th in the nation with 273.1 yards allowed per game MORE: How tight ends, backs can help the worst passing game in the Sarkisian-era Texas vs Missouri key matchup Texas cornerback Warren Roberson vs. Missouri receiver Cayden Lee Veteran Warren Roberson, who has played in 36 career games for the Longhorns, could get his first career start for the Longhorns' banged-up corners. It's a daunting debut, since Missouri's Cayden Lee leads the SEC with 756 yards receiving on 53 catches. Texas vs Missouri prediction Thomas Jones: Missouri 23, Texas 20. Texas has a history of playing well in big games under head coach Steve Sarkisian, but can the Longhorns find the needed emotional spark in their first conference visit to this SEC hinterlands? It's the game of the year for many Mizzou fans; it feels like a trap for Texas. Danny Davis: Texas. The Longhorns are solidly back in the CFP conversation and will remain so even if the defense has to carry them to another win this weekend in Columbia as injuries and inefficiencies continue to haunt the UT offense. Cedric Golden: Texas 24, Missouri 21. The Longhorns are beaten up and understand how essential this win will be to their postseason hopes. They have a much better chance of beating Missouri than they do of winning at LSU next week. They take advantage and eek out a win, thanks again to the defense. Michael Shapiro: Texas 20, Missouri 19. Texas' defense will stiffen in the red zone against a strong Missouri run game, and Arch Manning will continue to churn yards on the ground in a grinding, just-effective-enough afternoon for the Longhorns' offense. This is life in the SEC. It might not be pretty, but every win is another point of evidence for Steve Sarkisian as he makes Texas' case for inclusion in the College Football Playoff. picks.blurb: No. 7 Texas vs. No. 18 Missouri preview: Tigers host Longhorns for top 25 battle | Burnt Orange Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Texas Longhorns Community Burnt Orange Nation November 5, 2026 Burnt Orange Nation Notifications Notifications Get The App Sections Texas Longhorns Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Texas Football Odds Texas Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search Get The App Sections Expand Texas Longhorns Recruiting Betting Expand Betting News All communities Notifications Texas Longhorns Football A balanced Tiger team hosts the Longhorns for a top-25 matchup on Saturday. Boasting a 6-2 record and Top 25 ranking, the No. 19 Missouri Tigers host the No. 7 Texas Longhorns this Saturday in a matchup with huge implications for both teams. With identical records overall and in conference play, this matchup will be a reality check for postseason expectations for both squads. Win, and the path to the playoffs remain wide open. Lose, and the rest of the season could be tough to overcome. Missouri began the season with a 3-0 record that included a win over rival Kansas, but then fell at the hands of Mississippi State 31-24 in a close battle on the road. The Tigers bounced back with a 45-17 thrashing of Florida and a 27-6 win over Texas A&M. With a 5-1 record, Missouri was starting to get national attention. However, Ole Miss pumped the brakes on that narrative in a 31-3 victory. The Tigers failed to score on any drive after the opening series and elite running back Jamal Roberts was held to less than two yards per carry on 20 touches. The Rebel defense also forced quarterback Austin Simmons to throw 44 passes, a formula that Muschamp will likely seek to repeat. The Tigers bounced back last week with a 34-10 win over Arkansas while forcing four turnovers. Missouri brings a stingy defense and talented offense to the table. The Tigers rank fifth in the SEC in scoring defense, one spot behind the Longhorns, while their rushing and passing attacks both slot at sixth or better. Texas has the defensive personnel to make Missouri struggle, but limiting quarterback Austin Simmons and running back Jamal Roberts will not be easy. The Tigers also boast the most productive wide receivers in the conference in Cayden Lee. The Longhorn defense has to plug the run game, something that the Tigers rely on heavily. On the other side of the ball, Texas will need to win through the air. Missouri gives up less than 100 yards per game on the ground, a stellar number, but can be susceptible through the air. They’ve been able to create turnovers, so winning that battle will also be crucial. No matter how you spin it, this matchup will require a strong showing from Texas. Missouri took a step back last season but appears poised to return to the success they found under head coach Eli Drinkwitz in 2023 and 2024. Now in his seventh season, Drinkwitz has Missouri on the doorstep of competing with the traditional powers in the SEC. His offensive background has flourished in recent years, including this one, and the team has shown to be a resilient bunch with impressive wins after both losses. Here’s how the Tigers stack up position by position. The Tiger offense has been remarkably efficient this season and features one of the best running backs in the country in Jamal Roberts, the engine of the offense and that allows quarterback Austin Simmons to find ample space down the field. Stopping the fourth best run game in the SEC and making the offense one dimensional will be a key for the Longhorn defense. Quarterback Austin Simmons leads the offense for the Tigers. The transfer quarterback is in his first season with Missouri after spending three years in Oxford with Ole Miss. He’s taken a winding road to this season that began as a dual-sport athlete. Originally expected to be a member of the 2025 high school class, Simmons reclassified to 2023, ending his high school career two years early to pursue both football and baseball as the Division 1 level. He took classes year round and completed an associate degrees at age 17 with an impressive GPA, giving him the academic credentials necessary to enroll two years ahead of schedule. As a Rebel, Simmons sat behind NY Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart before taking over the starting job in 2025. An ankle injury forced him to miss time which gave current Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss the chance to start, a role he never relinquished. Simmons transferred this past offseason. With great size and an accurate lefty motion, Simmons has put together a clean campaign this year. He’s completed 152-of-240 passes (63.3 percent) for 16 touchdowns and most importantly, just two interceptions. This season, he’s been feast or famine despite the efficiency, throwing for 290 yards or more in four contests but less than 180 in three others. Simmons isn’t particularly dangerous as a runner. He’s best working off play action, so stopping the run game and forcing him into obvious passing situations will help limit his effectiveness. Heading into the season, first-team All-American Ahmad Hardy was expected to continue his dominant 2025 season. An emergency surgery in the offseason due to a gunshot wound at a concert forced Hardy to miss the beginning of the season, but the star returned last week for the first time, carrying the ball twice for five yards. He’s still reaching 100-percent health, but is expected to get some handoffs on Saturday. Hardy’s absence opened the door for Roberts, who leads the SEC in rush yards per game and ranks third in the FBS with 1,005 yards. Roberts was an impressive second option last season, tallying 753 yards on 124 carries, and has taken full advantage of Hardy being sidelined. He put up 211 yards against Florida and followed it up the next week with 222 against A&M. Roberts will see a healthy dose of carries, likely somewhere around 25, as well as a few passes out of the backfield. He can turn a routine play into extra yards with his physical running style and break off huge runs with his acceleration and top end speed. Shutting him down is the biggest task for the Texas defense and arguably one of the most important factors of the game. Wide receiver Missouri’s offense is run centric, but features Cayden Lee, the most productive wide receiver in the SEC. He spent three seasons in Oxford with Simmons before the duo elected to transfer to Missouri together. What a recruiting win that turned out to be for Drinkwitz. Lee is electric. At 5’11, 180 pounds, Lee isn’t a huge target. However, he has a great feel for finding space and creating explosive plays from the slot. He converts first downs and catches everything, making him an extremely reliable receiver. He’s leading the SEC with 756 yards receiving and second in catches with 53. The other wide receiver to know is sophomore Donovan Olugbode. A bigger target at 6’2, 210 pounds, Olugbode has reeled in 40 catches for 584 yards and seven touchdowns in seven games. He missed the A&M game in early October, but returned to catch nine passes for 127 yards against Ole Miss, as well as a touchdown last week. Solely bracketing Lee is not possible with what Olugbode can do. Each requires attention, and can wreck a secondary, especially when the run game pulls extra defenders to the line of scrimmage. The tight end for the Tigers is senior Brett Norfleet, who has impressive size at 6’6, 255 pounds, and has recorded nine catches for 80 yards and a touchdown this season. He’s an experienced player with 1,400+ snaps in the past three seasons. Offensive line The Missouri offensive line has been solid this year, creating holes for Roberts and time for Simmons. This group was forced to replace three of the five starters, but has hardly missed a beat this year. Leading the way is 2025 first-team All-SEC left tackle Cayden Green, one of the conference’s best bookends. He’s joined by a host of other reliable options that have experience and talent. This group rarely gives up sacks and has imposed their will against every team other than Ole Miss. It is one of the best the Longhorns will face all season. The Missouri offense is capable across the board. It starts up front with a reliable front five that has allowed Roberts to establish himself as one of the best in the country. His success has opened space in the secondary and the play-action offense, giving Simmons room to operate. He’s got two skilled wide receivers to throw to, creating a well-balanced unit that has performed well this season. The Tigers struggled against Ole Miss, a formula that Texas will undoubtedly look to recreate on Saturday. Missouri’s defense has arguably been the more consistent unit. It has been extremely effective against the run and generated turnovers at a high rate. It ranks top 30 in the country in many areas and has looked salty, excluding the Ole Miss game. However, the secondary has given up yards through the air, meaning this game could fall on the shoulders of the offensive line creating time and Manning delivering accurate passes. Defensive line Leading the way up the middle are Marquis Gracial and Jalen Marshall. Gracial tallied 257 snaps for Missouri in 2025 and has been effective against the run. Marshall bring great size at 6’4, 335 pounds and experience. He saw 342 snaps last year. Donta Simpson is another guy coming off injury that will provide a presence inside. The group of defensive ends is strong. A trio of Daeden Hopkins, Darris Smith, and Langdon Kitchen give Missouri depth to keep fresh legs. Hopkins shined brightest earlier in the season with 6.5 sacks in his first three games, but has since cooled off and will come off the bench. Smith is coming off an injury and saw his highest snap count in a month last week. He recorded three hurries and recovered a fumble last week. This unit has been hurt by injuries but can still get after it. They’re effective against the run and have depth that brings talent off the bench. The Missouri linebacker duo is made up by junior Nicholas Rodriguez and senior Robert Woodyard Jr. Rodriguez came into the season as the most veteran linebacker on the team after playing 352 snaps last season, which was the third most on the team. He was graded as a highly-effective run stopper according to Pro Football Focus — 86.4 run defense and 78.4 tackling. This season, he’s leading the tram with 88 tackles, 20 more than the next closest. He’s also added four quarterback hits and two forced fumbles. Next to him, Woodyard has emerged as another transfer recruiting win for Drinkwitz. After spending three seasons at Auburn, Woodyard opted to keep his mascot the same but suit up in black and gold instead. He’s been a much needed addition to the Missouri defense, posting 49 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss, an interception, and forced fumble. Rodriguez is the centerpiece of this unit and the defense as a whole. He’s active and productive. Texas should test these two with screens and misdirection early in the game, something opposing offenses have keyed on. The cornerback position was hit hard this offseason and forced to replace three starters from last season. To combat the lack of experience, Missouri turned to the portal bringing in a host of players to compete for the starting jobs. Fifth-year transfer Chris Graves secured one of the spots after starting nine games for Ole Miss last season while Sione Laulea, who spent last season with Oregon, will see most of the snaps at the other spot. Both possess good size. Graves brings much more experience than anyone else on the backend and arrived with Simmons and Lee. Another corner to know is Jahlil Florence, a physical corner who has been unable to play much the last few seasons due to injury. Smothers has battled injuries throughout the season, his first with the Longhorns . He had just four carries in last week's win over the Mississippi State Bulldogs, finishing with -6 yards. He missed their games against the Oklahoma Sooners and Ole Miss Rebels earlier in the season. He is second on the team with 69 carries for 283 yards and two touchdowns, averaging 4.1 yards per carry. Raleek Brown has taken on a bigger workload with Smothers limited and leads the team in carries (92), yards (452), touchdowns (5), and yards per carry (4.9). The Texas Longhorns ' brutal injury luck just got worse. Starting running back Hollywood Smothers is set to miss the rest of the 2026 season with an injury, according to On3's Pete Nakos . Smothers was one of Texas' top additions this offseason after two excellent seasons with the NC State Wolfpack. He was ranked as the No. 3 running back in the transfer portal by 247Sports, but his injuries have prevented him from getting going. At 6-2, Texas has a path to make the College Football Playoff after debuting as the No. 7 team in the initial rankings. They will close the season against the No. 18 Missouri Tigers, No. 14 LSU Tigers , Arkansas Razorbacks, and Texas A&M Aggies. Ahead of Saturday's matchup agaisnt Mississippi State, Simmons received a somewhat surprising designation of "questionable" on the initial injury report before being downgraded to "doubtful" on Thursday. He joins Goosby and defensive end Richard Wesley as the only three Longhorns that are officially out against Mississippi State. home.headline: Missouri football injury updates on official SEC report Wednesday before Texas
home.blurb: Mizzou published its first of four SEC-mandated availability and injury reports on Wednesday, Nov. 4, ahead of its game this coming Saturday against Texas, and added no new names to begin the week. That marks the second straight week that the Tigers have opened a game week without any injury concerns beyond players previously ruled out for the year. The major injury news comes out of Austin, Texas, as the Longhorns listed multiple starters and key players with availability designations. On offense for Texas, starting wideouts Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo were listed as questionable, and rotational running back Hollywood Smothers has been ruled out. On defense for the Longhorns, star defensive end Colin Simmons is questionable. Starting nickel Graceson Littleton and cornerback Kade Phillips, who have played the fifth- and sixth-most defensive snaps for the Longhorns this season, respectively, also were questionable. As it has since SEC play started, Mizzou ruled out running back Malae Fonoti, who is out for the season, right tackle Josh Atkins, who Eli Drinkwitz said he does not expect to be available this year, and tight end Gavin Hoffman. EDG #1 Colin Simmons (Questionable) WR #1 Ryan Wingo (Questionable) WR #8 Cam Coleman (Questionable) DB #8 Kade Phillips (Questionable) DB #29 Graceson Littleton (Questionable) The possible designations, from most likely to play to least likely, are as follows: available; probable; questionable; doubtful; out. The reports are not technically injury reports, which some teams — Mizzou often included — provided in years prior. Instead, they are lists that include any players ruled unavailable or possibly unavailable for upcoming games. That could be for any number of reasons, including but not limited to injuries. home.headline: Texas Gets Devastating Hollywood Smothers Injury Update Ahead of Missouri
home.blurb: Texas RB Hollywood Smothers Out for Rest of Season Texas Gets Devastating Hollywood Smothers Injury Update Ahead of Missouri Skip to main content SI.COM The Texas Longhorns have been no stranger to the injury bug this season, though this hasn't stopped the team from being firmly in the College Football Playoff race. Already without starting left tackle Trevor Goosby for the remainder of the season, the injury issues have piled up for Texas headed into Saturday's road matchup with the Missouri Tigers. Now, the Longhorns are receiving worst-case scenario news when it comes to starting running back Hollywood Smothers, who exited last week's game against Mississippi State with an apparent lower-body injury. Texas Longhorns running back Hollywood Smothers (2) warms up before a game against the UTSA Roadrunners at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Smothers will miss the remainder of the 2026 season due to a torn MCL in his knee, according to multiple reports. He started the year off as the team's starter after transferring in from NC State. Smothers will miss the remainder of the 2026 season due to a torn MCL in his knee, according to multiple reports. He started the year off as the team's starter after transferring in from NC State. In the second half against Mississippi State, Smothers took a hard hit to his lower body and sat on the turf holding his left knee. He was then helped off the field by trainers and was unable to put any weight on his left leg. Smothers finishes his 2026 season with 69 carries for 283 yards and two touchdowns along with 10 catches for 79 yards and another score. His pair of rushing touchdowns came in one of the biggest moments of Texas' season, as he had two scores in the fourth quarter against Ohio State, highlighted by the game-winning touchdown in the final minute to complete the comeback. The Longhorns have already gotten accustomed to life without Smothers this season. He previously dealt with ankle and shoulder injuries, forcing him to miss games against Tennessee and Ole Miss. Texas running back Raleek Brown now becomes the no-doubt starter moving forward for the Longhorns. So far this season, he's tallied 92 carries for 452 yards and five touchdowns along with 12 catches for 54 yard and another score. This was highlighted by an impressive performance in the win over Ole Miss when he had 23 carries for 157 yards. Behind him, Michael Terry III and Derrek Cooper will continue to receive an uptick in snaps. Terry has impressed and appears to have overtaken Cooper on the depth chart. It feels likely Terry will be Brown's backup moving forward. No. 7 Texas and No. 18 Missouri will kickoff from Columbia on Saturday at 11 a.m. CT. picks.headline: Gophers-UCLA preview: Minnesota has another golden opportunity to pull off a major upset
picks.source: Bring Me The News on MSN
picks.blurb: The Gophers nearly pulled off one of the biggest upset wins in modern program history against No. 4 Indiana, but they fell just short in overtime. No. 5-ranked UCLA now comes to Minneapolis, and Minnesota has a golden opportunity to bounce back with another upset win. Here’s what you need to know. From the practice field: What we’re hearing Minnesota’s 2026 regular season has been an emotional roller coaster, and the Gophers now face a truly heartbreaking low after nearly knocking off the Hoosiers. How they respond will determine how the rest of the season feels. “I think this team has a really unique ability to peel the logo and ranking off of them. They didn’t care. They went in there and played their guts out. They played their guts out against Michigan; they played their guts out against Iowa. This one just didn’t go our way. You’re not going to win them all,” P.J. Fleck said on Tuesday. “This week is no different. Peel the logo back, peel the ranking back. Go play our best football game of the year. It’s all I can ask out of our football team.” The matchup-specific stat that matters Minnesota has already faced three defenses ranked inside the top 12 in total yards allowed per game. Michigan is currently No. 3, Indiana is No. 6 and Iowa is No. 12. UCLA is allowing 260.8 yards per game, which ranks seventh in the country. The Bruins are allowing 87.2 rushing yards per game, which ranks 10th, and 173.5 passing yards per game, which ranks 14th. First-year head coach Bob Chesney is a heavy favorite to win national coach of the year, and his decision to bring defensive coordinator Colin Hitschler with him from James Madison has paid off. If there are any hopes of Minnesota’s offense making massive improvements, they might not happen this week against the Bruins. Injury/availability report The Gophers got defensive tackle Riley Sunram back from injury against Indiana, but tight end Pierce Walsh and versatile defensive back Garrison Monroe were out against the Hoosiers. Both Walsh and Monroe have a chance of returning this week, and it’s worth monitoring the status of defensive tackle Naquan Crowder, who played a season-low 11 snaps against Indiana. UCLA has started backup quarterback Ty Dieffenbach for the last three games since Nico Iamaleava suffered a season-ending injury against Oregon. But UCLA and Minnesota have dealt with their fair share of injuries this season. Head-to-head history and recent trends The Gophers have faced UCLA four times, including the 1961 Rose Bowl. They then had a home-and-home nonconference series in 1977 and 1978. They most recently played in 2024 in California, and Minnesota won that game 21-17. The more compelling trend is Minnesota’s recent history as a home underdog. The Gophers already have wins over Michigan and Iowa in that spot this season, and they beat Nebraska in that spot last season and USC in 2024. Fleck knows how to motivate his team for moments like the one they’ll have on Saturday. Whether or not that results in another upset win and field storm remains to be seen. X-factor: Minnesota’s offense Football doesn’t always have to be complicated. UCLA’s offense has had its fair share of struggles, scoring no more than 28 points in a single game since September. I fully expect the Gophers’ defense and special teams to have them in Saturday’s game until the very end. The outcome will come down to whether Minnesota’s offense can make enough plays . Drake Lindsey has struggled for a month, and pressure is building on offensive coordinator Greg Harbaugh Jr. to deliver better results. Coaching tendencies Chesney has become one of the fastest-rising head coaches in football. He was the head coach of Division III Salve Regina in 2012, and he has quickly gone from there to Division II Assumption College, then FCS Holy Cross, James Madison for two years, and now UCLA, which he has made a Big Ten title contender overnight. The comparison to Curt Cignetti’s meteoric rise at Indiana has been made ad nauseam, but the reality is that Chesney is already one of the best coaches in the sport. He hires at a high level, knows how to develop talent, and the Bruins are legit. Minnesota connections UCLA doesn’t have a player from Minnesota on its roster or a transfer from the Gophers program. The coaching staff has a lot of East Coast flavor, with Chesney being from Pennsylvania. There are zero major Minnesota connections with the UCLA program. Weather forecast After a rainy week in Minneapolis, it should feel like real fall weather for Saturday’s 11 a.m. kickoff . The current forecast calls for temperatures in the low 40s by the time the game starts, which could climb into the 50s by the fourth quarter. The Bruins will get a chilly Minnesota welcome for their first trip to the Land of 10,000 Lakes since 1977. away.headline: UCLA Gets Major Update From QB Nico Iamaleava After Season-Ending Injury
away.blurb: Iamaleava seemed to have settled in nicely with the Bruins program and first-year head coach Bob Chesney, helping the program get out to a 4-0 start to the year before suffering a torn ACL in the first half of their Week 6 win over Oregon. UCLA will look to keep their undefeated record alive in Iamaleava's absence for the rest of the season. But moving forward, Iamaleava seems to intend to return to the UCLA program next season. According to CBS Sports College Football insider Matt Zenitz, Iamaleava has indicated to the Bruins that he plans to return to UCLA next season instead of potentially trying his hand at entering the 2027 NFL Draft. The decision to return back to college for Iamaleava is a fairly obvious one. Not only would NFL scouts be taking a significant risk potentially drafting a quarterback coming off a torn ACL injury. But it would also allow for Iamaleava to produce more film for scouts for the 2028 NFL Draft. away.headline: UCLA’s ‘Heartbroken’ Nico Iamaleava Makes Career Announcement After Season-Ending Injury
away.blurb: The setback came during UCLA's win over Oregon on October 10. After being tackled by two defenders, the quarterback appeared to twist his left leg. He briefly returned to the game but did not come back after halftime. The injury was later confirmed to be a torn ACL, ending his season after just five starts. Now, UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava has made his intentions for the future clear. Rather than moving to the NFL, the senior reportedly plans to return to the Bruins for the 2027 season. The news of Iamaleava's expected return was shared by CBS Sports reporter Matt Zenitz, who cited the quarterback's agent, Rudy Caamano. In a post on X, Zenitz wrote, "UCLA star quarterback Nico Iamaleava has indicated to the Bruins that he plans to return to UCLA next season instead of leaving for the NFL, his agent @RudyCaamano of @AiC_Athletes tells @CBSSports." Zenitz also pointed out that Iamaleava had been emerging as a potential first-three-round selection in the 2027 NFL draft before suffering the injury. This is not the first time Iamaleava or UCLA has faced a major injury setback. During his time at Tennessee, Iamaleava dealt with minor physical hits that briefly sidelined him, but a full ACL recovery presents a new test. However, UCLA has seen quarterbacks successfully return from major knee surgeries before, giving both the program and the player a clear road map for recovery before he takes the field again in 2027. His progress could also make the quarterback situation worth watching next season. Iamaleava's expected return would give the Bruins an experienced option, but Dieffenbach could have a say in the competition if he continues to perform well. UCLA has also secured a commitment from four-star quarterback Josiah Boyd, adding another name to the mix for 2027. For UCLA, his expected return could bring valuable experience to the quarterback room. However, the team's plans will also depend on how the other quarterbacks develop and how Iamaleava progresses during his recovery. The injury has put his 2026 campaign on hold, but it has not ended his college career. As Iamaleava made clear in his Instagram post, he intends to return. The next chapter now points toward 2027, when he will have another opportunity to take the field for the Bruins. away.blurb: In an Instagram post, the UCLA quarterback acknowledged that he would be unable to return this season after getting crunched by two defenders earlier this month against Oregon. With another season of eligibility remaining, Iamaleava could return to college in 2027 after a shaky start to this season with the Bruins. In parts of five games, Iamaleava completed 62.1% of his passes for 982 yards with 4 touchdowns and 4 interceptions. The loser of this game may miss out on the college football playoff and given the Tigers' remaining strength of schedule, this is a must-win for LSU. Both teams are coming off a bye week, so we should expect a chess match between Lane Kiffin and Kalen DeBoer . Some would say this is a must-win for Alabama despite being the #5 ranked team in the new playoff rankings. The Tide's two best wins came against Kentucky when the Wildcats were unranked and a routing of #16 Mississippi State which sent Kamario Taylor and the program into a spiral. A win at LSU would solidify Alabama's spot, but a loss puts their season in the hands of others. Alabama plays Vanderbilt, Chattanooga, and Auburn following LSU; one of the easiest strength of schedules in P4. Alabama trailed 20-17 to Texas A&M before rattling off 14 points in the fourth quarter to avoid three-straight losses. Keelon Russell threw for 311 yards and three touchdowns, and the defense forced three turnovers in the win. Alabama has won three straight against LSU and won 12 of the last 15. Sam Leavitt and Kiffin will try to break the streak in his debut season. LSU is coming off two back-to-back big wins before the bye week. The Tigers crushed Mississippi State 31-0 and Auburn 38-17. Sam Leavitt threw seven touchdowns and ran for another in that two-game span, plus Jackson Harris caught four of those touchdowns and totaled 263 receiving yards. LSU's defense has only allowed 281 yards through the air in those two games as well, so nothing should come easy in Death Valley for one of the best home defenses in the country. Let's dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. picks.blurb: Alabama Football 2026 vs. LSU: Previewing the Tiger Defense - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Alabama Football 2026 vs. LSU: Previewing the Tiger Defense AUBURN, ALABAMA - OCTOBER 24: Quarterback Byrum Brown #17 of the Auburn Tigers passes the ball during the first half of an NCAA football game against the LSU Tigers at Jordan Hare Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Auburn, Alabama. (Photo by Stew Milne/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brent Taylor · SB Nation Thu, November 5, 2026 at 2:35 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For all of the things that didn't go right in the Brian Kelly era at LSU, the hiring of Blake Baker to be the defensive coordinator was a game changer for the Tigers, and even after changing head coaching regimes, Lane Kiffin elected to keep Baker around to continue leading up that side of the ball. If you're interested, Cody Alexander at Matchquarters.com has a cool piece from this offseason on Baker's scheme. It's partially paywalled, but still has a free intro, and honestly, this site is worth a subscription anyway. LSU defensive coordinator Blake Baker runs one of the most aggressive pressure systems in the country, with a near-50% Pass Blitz Rate (PBR), ranking seventh in the Power 4. That high-pressure approach is built into Baker's schematic DNA, tracing back to his roots in the coaching tree of current Duke head coach Manny Diaz. Having worked under Diaz at Texas, Louisiana Tech, and Miami, Baker reflects his mentor's approach by avoiding passive four-man rushes and instead relying on heavy blitz packages to dictate terms to opposing offenses consistently. The Tigers' defense is unique, though, in that it operates within a structural paradox. LSU has always been able to carry elite defensive back play. Man coverage has been a main tool for most defensive coordinators in Baton Rouge. Even the zone-dominant Dave Aranda played mostly "Wizard 1" ( four-man rush with Cover 1 ) during his tenure. On standard downs, LSU ranked sixth among the Power 4 in Cover 1 usage (34%), with Cover 3 accounting for another 35% of the pie. Varied split field coverages made up the rest. Coverage, for the most part, was not an issue, which is why the Cover 1 numbers were so high, but the pass rush was. LSU only recorded 24 total sacks, ranking 100th in Sack%. On passing downs, Baker had to consistently amplify the rush by sending numbers. The metrics validate his efficiency as a blitz designer: Unblocked Pressures (UBP): 5th in the FBS, proving schematic manipulation over raw physical wins. When LSU blitzed, Baker understood how to attack the protections. Average Time To Pass (ATTP): 16th in the FBS at 2.36 seconds, forcing the ball out before routes could develop. When LSU blitzed, the pressure got there fast, only amplifying an already stout secondary. Though LSU operates one of the most aggressive systems in the country, sending five or more rushers on 70% of its blitzes, Baker leans heavily into "safe" zone coverages rather than exposing his secondary in man coverage. When sending numbers, the Tigers completely flip from a man-match defense to pure zone. LSU's structural shift cuts its standard Cover 1 usage to 30% while flooding the backend with Fire Zone coverage on 52% of pressure downs. Now, for what it's worth, there have been some frustrations with Baker's defense this year. They've mostly dominated their overmatched competition, but they gave up 32 points and 35 points in losses to Ole Miss and Kentucky. Passing defense was a big problem for them against the Rebels, while the Wildcats were able to hang a bunch of yards in both the passing and the rushing game on them. Outside of those two games, though, they've been stellar. And most impressively, they're 4th in the country in "havoc rate", with 22.2% of their defensive plays being a tackle for loss, forced fumbled, pass deflection, or interception. If you like advanced catch-all metrics, their defense is #2 in the country in FPI while they are #5 in the country in SP+. The main place they've struggled is their rushing defense consistency. They get a lot of tackles for loss, but when they don't, they're 80th in the country at giving up explosive runs, and the overall EPA per play on rushing plays is in the bottom half. Essentially, they're extremely aggressive up front while simultaneously playing safe zone coverages on the back end, and it lends to big rushing plays if the team can get around that initial punch into the backfield. The big names on this LSU defense are right up front, with edge rushers Princewill Umanmielen and Jordan Ross both transferring in after big years at Ole Miss and Tennessee in 2025. Umanmielen has been arguably the best edge rusher in the country this year, with 8.5 sacks and 12 tackles for loss already this season, while Ross isn't far behind at 5 sacks and 9.5 TFLs. With those two commanding so much attention on the edges, true freshman defensive tackle Deuce Geralds has stepped up in the middle and has 5 sacks of his own from the interior. At linebacker, star inside backer Whit Weeks has been out for over a month with an injury, and while many thought that this would be the game he returned to action after a bye week, Weeks was listed as doubtful on LSU's injury report yesterday. In his stead are Davhon Keys and TJ Dottery, both smaller, speedy linebackers, but both played plenty of SEC snaps a year ago and are more than competent at the position. The defensive backfield is pretty much the only part of the LSU team that wasn't built through the transfer portal. DJ Picket is a 6'4" corner who was a freshman All-American last year as a rotational piece and has now moved into a full time starting role, leading the team with 7 pass breakups so far.. He's bookended by the much smaller 170-pound PJ Woodland, who was a solid starter for LSU all year last year. At the back end, Tamarcus Cooley returns to resume his starting role from last year. Redshirt freshman Jhase Thomas is the one guy in the crew that's getting his first real starting action this season. Finally, the nickelback is Ty Benefield, a first team All-MWC player for Boise State a year ago who's a physically imposing 6'3" 216 hybrid DB. He's third on the team with 33 tackles. Honestly, I don't love this matchup for the Alabama offense. To this point, Keelon Russell hasn't consistently shown he can beat a team willing to blitz him without relying on his ability to make a man miss, and I'm not sure these are the caliber of athletes that Russell can just consistently make free rushers miss him. Their biggest weakness is an overaggressiveness that can lead to some big runs or some good quick passing game – and to this point Alabama has only intermittently been able to do the first and really hasn't been able to do the latter at all this season. If the Tide can really get their counter run game going again like they were earlier in the season, then that's likely their best chance to score points. Basically – follow the second half game plan from the Kentucky game. The problem is, have we seen them with the patience to do that ever since? I'm not sure. I don't have a great feeling about this one. The Tide offense has a lot of growing up to do this week if they want to prove they deserve a #5 ranking. And sure, getting Ryan Coleman-Williams, Racin Delgatty, and EJ Crowell healthy (hopefully) should make a big difference compared to what we've seen the past few weeks, but we also need to see a lot of improvement from Russell, Ryan Grubb, and the group as a whole if we're going to see Alabama pull of a win. My best guess? 24 points for the Tide.

Alabama was without wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams, cornerback Zabien Brown, running back EJ Crowell, center Racin Delgatty and nose tackle Terrance Green during the home win over Texas A&M on Oct. 24. All of them being questionable shows some progress, as head coach Kalen DeBoer provided an update on the group during Monday's press conference. "A lot of these guys from Zabien Brown to Ryan Coleman-Williams, EJ, Racin, Terrance Green in particular, those guys are all working onto the football field," DeBoer said . "They're not all in the exact same spot, but they're all out there going through workouts. Some are taking team reps, some are taking non-contact reps. "But I think the progress by all of them is headed in a good direction. We'll see. I think a lot of it has to do with how their bodies respond after they're out there being pushed a little bit more." Will Sanders: lower-extremity – sustained against Texas A&M and is out for a couple of weeks "Guys are making good progress," DeBoer said. "I think that's what a lot of it was said on Monday. I know a lot of that report will be coming out here, as we have to do with the SEC report." Edge rusher Desmond Umeozulu hasn't played since the win over Florida State as he's been dealing with turf toe.
