away.blurb: Happy Thursday, everyone. The women’s basketball team moved to 2-0 on the season with a 118-45 drubbing of New Orleans last night. Ace Austin is the leader of the squad, but everyone got in on the scoring action in that one. The men return to action tomorrow night against Arkansas State. The initial injury report came out for LSU, and most of the guys that we hope to see back on the field on Saturday are listed as questionable. Alabama lists 7 players as questionable for LSU game It’s good to see Sanders on the questionable list, but it sounds like he will be out. Williams, Green, and Delgatty have been spotted in practice footage released this week, so there is hope for them. Lane Kiffin listed Whit Weeks as doubtful on the report but nobody is buying that. Whit has had this game circled for his return for Weeks now, pun intended. “Just all-around complete football team,” the head coach said. “You know, playing better and better football as they go. Thought the last game against Auburn was impressive. The way they came out right away, jumped on them and had a good first quarter and then obviously continued that into the third quarter too. So didn’t need to have to keep the pedal down too much there in the fourth. But just you know, quarterback. I mean, guys, skill players around him. They’re more and more on the same page. A defensive front, actually, a defense as a whole, that just plays well together. Gets pressure on the passer and they’re at the top of the SEC and national rankings in a lot of areas, both offensively and defensively. So you know they’re a complete team.” “It feels like all of us are winning when we see Ivan out there doing what he’s doing,” McFadden said. Hopefully the recent upsets continue and I have a reason to revisit this piece after the season. But for now, we’re only looking at a score of about 33 out of 50 on the 2007 scale. Granted, that might be as close as virtually any season of the last nearly two decades has come, but if nothing else, this exercise should have reminded us just how wacky 2007 really was. If all you got out of this exercise was a reminder of Les Miles’ ridiculousness and a search of “Pat White highlights” on YouTube , it was worth it. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 12 Ohio State hosts No. 23 Oregon in a pivotal game in the Big Ten and CFP race Getty Images Week 10 of the college football calendar has been highlighted since the schedule was released, with No. 23 Oregon's trip to face No. 12 Ohio State among the headliners. However, when the Buckeyes host the Ducks at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS, it will not be two teams vying for a bye in the College Football Playoff, but instead two programs trying to keep their season from unraveling. The Ducks, at 5-3, have already seen their playoff dreams snuffed out, but a win last week against Northwestern brought their offense to life after a coordinator change. Dylan Raiola had his best game as a starter for Oregon in a win over Northwestern, and now the Ducks have real belief they can go into the Horseshoe and pick up a win that could salvage what's been a disappointing season. Ohio State, meanwhile, comes in with a backup quarterback of their own and is searching for answers after a 30-18 loss on the road to USC last week. Luke Fahey will get his second start and first at home, hoping to find more success and keep Ohio State in the playoff hunt after the first CFP rankings put them at No. 12 -- which would be the first team out of the 12-team playoff. The winner on Saturday will enter the stretch run of the season feeling like they've stabilized after a shock to the system in the form of losing their star quarterbacks for the year. The loser, on the other hand, will realize their goals are no longer within reach and face some hard questions entering the offseason. Ohio State vs. Oregon: Need to know Can Ohio State solve red-zone woes?: The Buckeyes moved the ball fine against USC's defense. It was the best rushing performance from Ohio State this season in Big Ten play in terms of yards per carry (4.74), and while Fahey missed some explosives, he still threw for 260 yards. The problem for Ohio State was finishing drives with six points instead of three. Ohio State made four trips into the red zone against USC and came away with just 13 points. Against Indiana , it also scored 13 points in three trips to the red zone, and the inability to come away with touchdowns nearly cost them there too. If the Buckeyes are going to control this game and keep Oregon from building belief it can win on the road, Fahey has to be sharper in the red zone and the Ohio State rushing attack has to be able to help out. Ducks find life after coordinator change: Oregon's offense had its best performance since the win at USC last Saturday afternoon against Northwestern, one week after firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. Interim coordinator Jay Johnson seemed able to get Raiola into a rhythm and keep him there, something the Ducks have struggled with all season (even with Dante Moore ). The frustration after the Illinois game seemed to be an unwillingness to stick with what worked -- in that game, it was the rushing attack -- and against Northwestern, once they found some concepts that worked, they went back to the well until proven otherwise. That seems simple, but it's not always easy as a play-caller to not let your mind wander and get too cute trying to stay ahead of the defense. Johnson seems more comfortable just rolling with what works and being aggressive in any spot, which seems to have a trickle-down effect on Raiola and the offense, also playing with more comfort and aggression. That's going to be necessary against an Ohio State defense that is quite good but, as USC proved, can be hit for big plays. Oregon can't be afraid to take swings as a road dog, and last week's performance gives it some confidence it can do that effectively with Raiola. Which defense can steal possessions?: With a young quarterback and a red-zone offense that's struggling, the Buckeyes might need their defense to give them a spark. For as good as the Buckeyes have been defensively this season, they haven't been great at turning teams over. They have just four interceptions on the year (94th nationally) and are 48th in total turnovers forced at 11. Raiola has been prone to turnovers for his entire career dating back to Nebraska and will likely present a couple of opportunities -- either with interceptable balls or strip sacks -- for the Buckeyes to steal a possession or two. Ohio State has to capitalize on those chances if they want to help their sputtering offense. On the other side, the best way to make Ohio State tight in this one would be to pick off the young quarterback and make Ryan Day a bit anxious about letting the young man sling it. Oregon has nine interceptions this season (13th in the country), and if they can bait the freshman into an early mistake, it could alter the Buckeyes' game plan and give the Ducks an even better opportunity on the road. Ohio State should be able to run the ball well, and at home I would expect Fahey and the offense to operate a bit better in the red zone to put touchdowns on the board when they do move the ball. A Ducks offense trying to push it in the passing game should result in big plays (possibly for both teams), and this is a rare big game where I'm anticipating plenty of points. picks.blurb: Oregon Ducks’ Playoff Odds Offer A Twist Before Ohio State Skip to main content SI.COM Transfer Portal FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2024 FOOTBALL COMMITS SI.COM DUCKS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM DUCKS BB The Oregon Ducks are rolling into their premier matchup against the No. 11 Ohio State Buckeyes with momentum. Oregon took down another AP Top-25 team, the No. 20 Northwestern Wildcats, and finally found an offensive rhythm. But the 34-26 win doesn’t change the fact that a 6-2 Buckeyes squad vs. a 5-3 Ducks team presents a much different matchup than their No. 1 and No. 2 preseason rankings suggested. While Ohio State’s postseason ambitions are still alive, Oregon’s three losses may not have eliminated it yet, at least according to the ESPN Football Power Ranking (FPI). Oregon Ducks coach Dan Lanning | Darby Winter Oregon Ducks’ College Football Playoff Hopes Not Dead Yet Oregon Ducks’ College Football Playoff Hopes Not Dead Yet The Ducks are No. 12 in the Week 10 ESPN FPI. The FPI still gives Oregon a chance, albeit a low one, to make the College Football Playoff at 4.2 percent. Additionally, Oregon is provided a 2.8 percent chance to win the Big Ten, a 0.4 percent chance to make the National Championship and a 0.2 percent chance to win the National Championship. What’s notable about the FPI is that its favorable ranking of Oregon, even with the turbulent first two months of the season, could still set the Ducks up for a postseason berth if the committee sees it the same way. After all, the 2026 college football season has already featured a plethora of twists and turns. Oregon defensive lineman Matayo Uiagalelei | Darby Winter The No. 5 UCLA Bruins and the No. 6 Indiana Hoosiers are the only two teams in the Big Ten with less than two loses. Oregon would need to win out and hope that a few other games outside its control go its way. The No. 5 UCLA Bruins and the No. 6 Indiana Hoosiers are the only two teams in the Big Ten with less than two loses. Oregon would need to win out and hope that a few other games outside its control go its way. The Ducks’ strength of schedule appears to give them the benefit of the doubt. Every Oregon opponent so far, except the Portland State Vikings, is ranked within the top 50 of the ESPN FPI. Five of the Ducks’ first eight opponents have also been ranked inside the Top 25 at some point in 2026. So the chances of the Ducks playing anything besides a bowl game in December might seem like a pipe dream, but if the selection committee sees it the same way as the FPI, it's not impossible. Either way, it adds to the stakes of the upcoming game in Columbus. Big Ohio State Buckeyes Matchup on the Horizon The Buckeyes narrowly lost a 24-23 battle against the Texas Longhorns on Sept. 12 but bounced back in dominant fashion. It seemed that Ohio State was going to be a difficult team to beat a second time down the stretch of the season, especially after defeating the Hoosiers 19-15. But an unranked USC Trojans team that just came off an upset loss against the Wisconsin Badgers continued the chaos in the Big Ten by taking down the Buckeyes 30-18. Ohio State now enters the game against Oregon in a similar situation the Ducks were in after losing to the Bruins – a loss could end its hopes of returning to the CFP. The Buckeyes still have games against Northwestern, Nebraska and Michigan left on the schedule. The Ducks’ only two wins against the Buckeyes come in the last two regular season meetings, with last one at Autzen Stadium and the 2021 meeting in Columbus. Ohio State did, however, get the best of the Ducks the last time out in a 41-21 victory in the 2025 Rose Bowl. Ohio State at home, coming off its second loss of the season, is a dangerous matchup, but Oregon now has the opportunity to play spoiler for other teams' postseason desires. The Ducks (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten Conference) and Buckeyes (6-2, 4-1) both entered the season ranked in the top five in the major polls but find themselves scrapping to get their seasons back on track at Ohio Stadium this weekend. "Coach (Ryan) Day does an unbelievable job," coach Dan Lanning said. "It's a really well-coached team. They've got good personnel in all phases. They really show up, so it'll be a real challenge for us, but one that we're certainly excited about." Though freshman Luke Fahey has operated as the starter during Ohio State's bye week and loss to USC last week, OSU is still adjusting to life without its starting signal-caller. That's a huge advantage for an Oregon team that has settled in on its starter moving forward in Dylan Raiola and seemed to find its identity on offense in a win versus Northwestern. Why Ohio State has an advantage: No one has had an answer for Ohio State superstar and future NFL top-10 pick Jeremiah Smith. The junior has 62 catches for 1,067 yards and 13 touchdowns in eight games and is already the Big Ten's all-time leader in touchdown receptions in less than three seasons of play. Stopping Smith will be a massive challenge for the Ducks , who have shown to be susceptible against the passing game at points this season. Oregon vs. Ohio State injury updates Note: Official availability reports, mandated by the Big Ten, are released every day starting at 5 p.m. Wednesday leading up to kickoff. This story was published before the reports were made public. For Oregon: Several key Oregon contributors could return this week, though Lanning wouldn't talk about the specific status of any player during his Monday press conference and deferred to the Ducks' upcoming availability reports. Starting running back Jordon Davison was hobbled in the first half against Northwestern and was seen with crutches on the sideline in the second half, though Lanning said he didn't expect the injury to be long-term. For Ohio State: The biggest injury news for the Buckeyes revolves around Sayin, who is out for the foreseeable future since an injury versus Indiana in mid-October. Ohio State was also without standout freshman DB Jay Timmons and talented wideout Brandon Inniss vs. USC. Inniss was a game-time decision and participated in early warmups but did not play against the Trojans. Oregon outside linebacker Nasir Wyatt, left, brings down Northwestern quarterback Aidan Chiles as the Oregon Ducks host the Northwestern Wildcats on Oct. 31, 2026, at Autzen Stadium in Eugene, Oregon. Oregon vs. Ohio State: 4 bold predictions Oregon, Ohio State first half will be a defensive battle The Ducks rediscovered a bit of their old selves in a 38-point outing against a stout Northwestern defense last week, but the challenge will be greater this week, and the Ducks have yet to put together back-to-back good performances against good competition this season. That needs to change Saturday, but both teams, adjusting to new schemes and personnel, will get off to a slow start in Columbus this weekend. Ducks will hold Buckeyes' Jeremiah Smith under 100 yards Oregon has a good history of limiting opposing stars, though sometimes to a fault. Last season against future NFL draftee Makai Lemon and USC, the star had just 34 yards on seven catches in an Oregon win. But, that left Tanook Hines with the opportunity to cash in on the attention Lemon received. Lanning and his staff will have Smith circled everywhere, and they'll hold Smith under 100 yards, but Ohio State will still get production from other talents. Ohio State, Oregon game will come to down to field position, turnovers As most games do, Saturday's contest will come down to who commits more mistakes and who takes advantage of good field position. On the former front, Oregon has struggled mightily with protecting the ball. The Ducks have given the ball away 13 times this season, including 10 fumbles, while Ohio State has protected the ball slightly better but produces less turnovers on defense. Oregon punter Bailey Ettridge has been a massive weapon throughout the season, and if he can continually pin the Buckeyes deep, Oregon will have a good chance to spring the upset. It's all on the line in Columbus on Saturday when the Ohio State Buckeyes host the Oregon Ducks . Ohio State is very much playing for its chances in the College Football Playoff with two losses after falling to USC last weekend . Oregon already has three losses, but they've been playing better as of late. Ahead of the key Big Ten battle in Week 10, the college football staff has predictions on how Ohio State vs. Oregon is going to shake out. Ohio State 27, Oregon 20 The Buckeyes losing in Week 9 to USC stung so bad because it wasn't Julian Sayin's absence and starting a true freshman that did it. Luke Fahey played well enough to win that game and the rest of the team was a letdown for the most part. Ryan Day said everyone had to step up a little bit with a true freshman playing, but the opposite happened, with regression taking place. Flash forward a week and Ohio State's defense needs to get back on track against an Oregon team that's going to rely on its playmakers through the air. Dylan Raiola is going to get the ball to Dakorien Moore and tight end Jamari Johnson. Ohio State can't allow explosives as they did against USC, or it'll be another upset. I think Ohio State is going to respond at home in a way where they control this one the majority of the way, and fans feel a bit more at ease. - Brandon Little, A to Z Sports Ohio State Ohio State 27, Oregon 17 I'm taking Ohio State to defeat Oregon 27-17 in a matchup that has lost some of its luster, especially with both teams turning to backup quarterbacks. Still, I think the Buckeyes have a significant advantage defensively and will make life difficult for Oregon throughout the afternoon. Ohio State should be able to generate pressure, force some uncomfortable decisions and come up with several big plays that swing momentum. On the other side, freshman quarterback Luke Fahey shows some encouraging signs of growth. He won't be spectacular, but I expect him to look more comfortable and give Buckeye fans some reasons for optimism moving forward. Dylan Raiola will have his moments, making a few impressive throws and creating some explosive plays to keep Oregon within striking distance. However, the Ducks won't be able to find enough consistency offensively to keep pace. Ohio State's defense ultimately makes the difference, coming up with timely stops when Oregon needs answers most. Fahey does enough to help the Buckeyes put points on the board, and Ohio State controls the closing stages to secure a relatively comfortable win.- Ryan Roberts, A to Z Sports Notre Dame Ohio State 17, Oregon 16 Simply put, Ohio State is a much better team, but they aren't nearly good enough as of yet without Julian Sayin. The Ducks aren't doing much better, either, especially with Dante Moore not playing. The Ducks are reeling on multiple fronts, and Dan Lanning has many quesitoning his job performance. That will continue, as the Buckeyes find a way to win a dogfight. - Tyler Forness, A to Z Sports Florida Ohio State 20, Oregon 16 This is a very tough game to get a handle on, as both teams are riding with backup quarterbacks. Dylan Raiola bounced back last weekend against Northwestern looking more like the QB that helped the Ducks beat USC in Los Angeles. Speaking of LA, the Buckeyes struggled with Luke Fahey under center in a 30-18 loss to the Trojans. Jeremiah Smith did manage to log 10 catches, but he turned them into 83 yards and a touchdown, a relatively pedestrian total for him. This is a game that's an ugly offensive slog for much of the afternoon. Despite winning 34-26, the Ducks struggled against the run last week against the Wildcats, allowing 175 yards. Two weeks ago, Illinois went for 225 against Dan Lanning's team. The Buckeyes ran the ball well last week against USC with 204 rushing yards. The passing games don't work well for either team, but you can stamp US Mail on Bo Jackson and the OSU ground game on Saturday, which does just enough to eek out a close win. - Craig Smith, A to Z Sports Miami Ohio State 25, Oregon 15 This game is the season for the Ohio State Buckeyes. After losing quarterback Julian Sayin, a lot of people expected a big drop-off in Luke Fahey, but he was the last of the Buckeyes' problems last week against USC. The problem for Oregon is, they have been one of the biggest disappointments in the sport. Even before the season-ending injury to Dante Moore, the team was getting whooped in the trenches, and the coordinator changes fell flat. Now there are more questions than answers at quarterback, and they have to travel to Columbus to take on a Buckeyes team with their backs against the wall. That's a recipe for disaster for the Ducks in my opinion. The Buckeyes figure it out and start their win streak on Saturday. - Rob Gregson, A to Z Sports Alabama Ohio State 24, Oregon 17 I think Ohio State can still find a way to win this one, even with the situation they're currently in. They still have the best player in college football, maybe one of the best in Jeremiah Smith. They have to find a way to get the offense moving effectively and efficiently. The defense will handle the issues that Oregon creates for itself on offense. - Justin Churchill, A to Z Sports Oklahoma This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. away.headline: Ohio State football's Jay Timmons trending toward return against Oregon
away.blurb: Ohio State starting nickel back Jay Timmons is trending toward a return against Oregon on Nov. 7. Timmons, who was held out of last week’s loss at USC with an unspecified injury, was not included on the Buckeyes’ initial availability report released for their upcoming game against the Ducks. Timmons missed games against Iowa and Maryland earlier in October before returning at Indiana when he reaggravated his injury. He traveled with the Buckeyes to Los Angeles last week as he attempted to return but was ruled out near kickoff. Wide receivers Brock Boyd and Brandon Inniss were listed as questionable for Oregon after they were held out at USC. It was the second straight game Boyd was sidelined with an unspecified injury. Left tackle Ian Moore was also listed as questionable. Moore made a late exit against the Trojans as Austin Siereveld moved over from right tackle to replace him in the fourth quarter. Defensive tackle Eddrick Houston was not listed after he went down late last week and later limped off the field at the Coliseum, indicating he could be available against Oregon. This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: Ohio State football's Jay Timmons trending toward return against Oregon He has also practiced in recent days, prompting coach Ryan Day to express optimism about his status on Nov. 4. “We’ll have to see how the next 48 hours go,” Day said, “but he’s had two good days of practice. That would really inject a lot for us in the back end.” The Buckeyes’ secondary felt the absence of Timmons against the Trojans as they surrendered their longest passes this season between a 69-yard touchdown on the second play from scrimmage and another 70-yard reception in the third quarter. home.headline: Ryan Day says Ohio State QB Julian Sayin's recovery will take time
home.blurb: During his weekly radio show on 97.1 The Fan, Day said Sayin is making progress in his recovery, but it will take time before he is available for the Buckeyes. Sayin was previously ruled out indefinitely after suffering an injury at Indiana on Oct. 17 when defensive lineman Mario Landino came down on his right arm on a sack in the fourth quarter. Sayin has been at meetings with the Buckeyes and helped with installations. He was with teammates and staff on the sideline at the Los Angeles Coliseum when they visited USC and walked out with the team's captains for the opening coin toss. “It’s not going to be next week or next month,” Day said, “it's going to take some time, but certainly for the long term, we feel like we're on a good track.” He has continued to keep his right arm in a sling in recent weeks, including while he was with the Buckeyes at USC on Oct. 31. Day did not divulge specifics of the injury but seemed encouraged by the prognosis for the redshirt sophomore. “All things considered, the outcome with the different options thinking it could be, this has been a decent outcome for us and for him,” Day said. “We’ll let him go through that, but this thing looks to be healing.” Freshman Luke Fahey started in place of Sayin last week as the Buckeyes were upset by the Trojans and threw for 260 yards and one touchdown without an interception. Fahey will remain behind center as Ohio State hosts Oregon on Nov. 7. “It says a lot about him that he's not just doing his rehab,” Day said. “He's with the team. He takes his role very seriously.” Joey Kaufman covers Ohio State football for The Columbus Dispatch. Email him at jkaufman@dispatch.com and follow him on @joeyrkaufman on X.

home.headline: Three Oregon offensive injuries loom large entering pivotal Ohio State matchup
home.blurb: Jordon Davison appeared to get injured early in the game with an awkward hit on a screen pass from Dylan Raiola. Davison wasn't seen the rest of the 1st half, and when the team came back out for the 2nd half, he was spotting street clothes, and on a pair of crutches. Adding to the worries about Oregon's running back room was the fact that Dierre Hill Jr. looked hobbled during the game as well. The Ducks turned the room over to true freshman Brandon Smith who had his coming out party, to help save the day, but Hill missed most of the game. After the game, all that Dan Lanning added was that he was "a little banged up", so Oregon fans will be hoping for better news this week. When Oregon was trying to close out the game against Northwestern, it was troubling to see Dakorien Moore down after taking a big hit on the final punt return. Moore didn't return to the field for the final offensive series which is concerning, but it sounds like he'll be more than ready to go for the Ohio State game. In the long history of this rivalry, there's a good case that this is the biggest game ever. In his first year on the job, Will Stein has led Kentucky to a 7-1 start and a great shot at reaching the College Football Playoff with just four games remaining. His major transfer portal additions -- particularly quarterback Kenny Minchey and the offensive line -- clicked almost immediately. To this point, the Wildcats have passed all but one test they've faced, but the level of difficulty rises this weekend. Kentucky must continue to play clean football if it wants to come away with a win in Knoxville. Tennessee had two weeks to wallow in the "what if" after its three-point loss to South Carolina , but the team has to get back in the saddle this weekend. The Volunteers have the chance to pick up their second top-10 win of the season, which would really boost their CFP rankings. There's no doubt that the Vols have a playoff-caliber defense and running game, but can Josh Heupel fix the passing attack? Tennessee must improve there to reach its ceiling. Here is everything you need to know about this top-15 rivalry matchup in Knoxville. Tennessee vs. Kentucky: Need to know Rare ranked matchup: These teams have met well over 100 times, but this is just the fourth ranked matchup in history. Most recently, Tennessee and Kentucky played a top-25 matchup in 2022, with the Volunteers winning in a blowout. Prior to that, the only times the Vols and Wildcats were ranked simultaneously were in 1950 and 1951. That means there's a very good case for this matchup to be the biggest in the history of this rivalry. Games with stakes in this series usually go the way of Tennessee, but can Stein turn the tables on Saturday night? Kentucky not in the giving spirit: The holidays are approaching quickly, but Kentucky has not been feeling very generous. One of the driving factors behind the Wildcats' success is their incredible plus-13 turnover margin. That ranks first in the SEC and fourth in the entire country. For the first time since 2013, Kentucky has avoided turning the ball over in three consecutive games. If any team can end that streak, it's probably Tennessee, which has a great defense and has forced 14 turnovers in eight games. The Vols just have to protect the ball on offense. Heavy dose of DeSean Bishop : Kentucky defensive coordinator Jay Bateman probably doesn't need my advice, but I would suggest he lock in on Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop. He's been the engine of the Vols offense, and his 957 rushing yards rank sixth in the country. His 12 rushing touchdowns are tied for ninth. Over the last four games, Bishop has averaged 29 carries and 159 yards. If the Wildcats can contain Bishop and force Tennessee to throw the ball, that could be a recipe for success, but only one team has effectively shut Bishop down to this point. The Tennessee Vols are currently on the outside looking in at the 12-team College Football Playoff. Tennessee, which is 6-2 with four games remaining, was ranked No. 13 in the initial CFP rankings. The shocking part of Tennessee's ranking isn't that they were at No. 13 — we expected them to be in that range — it's that they were somehow ranked eight spots behind a two-loss Alabama team that lost by 16 points to the Vols a couple of weeks ago. Nearly everyone in college football media was shocked to see Alabama ranked that many spots ahead of the Vols. "Tennessee just whooped Alabama," said former Georgia quarterback Aaron Murray after the rankings were revealed. "I mean, they whooped Alabama. And you're going to tell me that Alabama is at No. 5 and Tennessee's at No. 13 in this ranking? I do not like Alabama at No. 5" The good news for the Vols is that they still control their own destiny. If Tennessee wins out in November, they'll secure a spot in the 12-team playoff. And that November journey begins this Saturday with a huge game against Kentucky in Neyland Stadium. Kentucky is ranked No. 6 in the initial College Football Playoff rankings. Murray, who called Tennessee's game against Arkansas for ESPN earlier this season, has the Vols beating the Wildcats 31-21 on Saturday. "I think George MacIntyre continues to mature in the offense," said Murray. "I have been really impressed with his growth as the starting quarterback over the past month, and he's got some really good receivers. Mike Matthews is electric with the football. They find creative ways to get him on skinny slants and quick screens to the outside. And I like the way they use DaSaahn Brame, the tight end. … He's very athletic and very fast, which is why him against (Kentucky linebacker) Grant Godfrey is gonna be very interesting in the pass game because both of those guys are long and can move. "But at the end of the day, I will continue to doubt Kentucky. I'm gonna do it myself again. I just had Kentucky, too, and I said I would stop doing it. But I like Tennessee. I like Tennessee a lot. I think Tennessee wins 31-21." Kentucky and Tennessee will kick off at 6:15 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ESPN. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. "We have a, you know, awesome opportunity this week to play an elite SEC opponent in Tennessee on the road. You know, I think they're playing extremely well as a team. They could easily be eight and zero. picks.headline: Tennessee offense preview: Can Kentucky force the Vols to pass?
picks.blurb: Tennessee offense preview: Can Kentucky force the Vols to pass? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Story by Wildcats Wire Tennessee offense preview: Can Kentucky force the Vols to pass? Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Wed, November 4, 2026 at 2:31 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels to Knoxville to face off against the #16 Tennessee Volunteers on Saturday night, and both teams are coming off of a bye week. We previewed the Tennessee defense and the big scheme showdown between Will Stein's offense against Jim Knowles' defense. Now we will take a look at the Tennessee offense that has consistently put up points under head coach Josh Heupel. Heupel's offense this year has struggled in some areas, and it has resembled the 2024 offense in a lot of ways. Since becoming the head coach of Tennessee in 2021, Josh Heupel has had his offense scoring a lot of points and he is 5-0 against Kentucky . Mark Stoops and Brad White could not figure out Heupel's up-tempo offense that features extremely wide splits from the wide receivers that creates a light box to run the football. Heupel's offenses are averaging over 40 points per game in this series. It is time to see if the new scheme change that has taken place under Jay Bateman will be more effective in slowing down this scheme. This scheme is creative because the wide splits create light boxes that the Vols will then use their ground game to run into favorable looks. Once Tennessee gets the run game going, they will then take shots down the field on deep option routes. However, this offense is similar to the 2024 version, which has become heavily dependent on the run game getting going. The quarterback situation is in the worst position it has been in under Heupel. Heupel is playing the cards close to his chest and continuing to use gamesmanship by not naming a starter. True freshman Faizon Brandon started the season and after struggling then getting a minor injury, the Vols switched to redshirt freshman George MacIntyre and have not switched back since. MacIntyre has ran the offense better in my opinion, he is less frantic in the pocket and is better at getting the ball out of his hands. The only issue is MacIntyre has not pushed the football down the field much, his 5.7 average depth of target is the lowest in the SEC and is obviously a critical element of Heupel's scheme. MacIntyre will get the start, but I wouldn't be surprised to see a little bit of Faizon Brandon as well to try and throw off Kentucky's defense. Kentucky has faced a dual threat quarterback every week of the season to this point, I am intrigued to see how this pass rush gets after a quarterback that is a pocket passer like MacIntyre. It is something we have yet to see, and this is an area that could be a massive advantage for the Wildcats. It is important that Kentucky wins the early downs on defense and force Tennessee to beat them through the air. Tennessee's offense is led by running back DeSean Bishop, and the Vols will absolutely try to feed him in this football game. Tennessee ranks third in the SEC in yards per rush and EPA per rush, they are very much a run heavy offense. Tennessee is still getting explosive plays in this offense, they have a 12.6 explosive play rate which is third in the conference. The Vols rank second in the SEC with a 15.3 explosive run rate and they rank 13th with a 9.6 explosive pass rate. Tennessee ranks 13th in the SEC in EPA per dropback and yards per pass attempt. They rank 11th in the conference with a 42.5% pass success rate. This is simple for Kentucky, stack the box and slow down this run game. Kentucky has to sell out to stop the run and force the Vols to beat them with their quarterbacks, whether it be MacIntyre or Brandon. DeSean Bishop is one of the best running backs in the country, he has 957 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns on the season. Bishop is averaging over 100 yards per game and 5.6 yards per carry. He helps the Vols convert on early downs, as their 46.5% early down conversion rate ranks sixth in the SEC. However, they have struggled to convert on third down like Kentucky as they have converted just 35.5% of third down opportunities this season, which ranks 15th in the SEC. In our self scout over the bye week, we pointed out how Kentucky's run defense really improved in the month of October. This has to continue for Kentucky to win this football game, but it will be easier said than done. Jay Bateman has to force Tennessee into a dropback heavy game by getting his defense to stop the run. If they can successfully do that, they will be in a great position to win this game. If you buy something from a link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement. CJ Baxter has had an injury-riddled career. At Texas, he sustained numerous injuries that kept him sidelined for varying lengths of time. When the elite tailback was on the field, his talent was very apparent, but keeping him there has always been the problem. In his time with the Kentucky Wildcats , he missed some in the preseason, some of it for precautionary reasons, but to start the actual season, he found himself playing some healthy football and playing really well. Before the Oklahoma game, Baxter got the OK to play but didn’t get time due to a soft tissue injury. Then, against Vanderbilt, he returned to the field briefly, logging just four snaps. He took a tough hit early in the contest and never returned to the field. Now, Kentucky has its biggest game yet on deck with the Tennessee Volunteers hosting Kentucky for its annual “Dark Mode” game at Neyland Stadium on Saturday night. So what’s the update on Baxter for this big road game? UK head coach Will Stein provided an update on Tuesday to clear the air on the Wildcats running back, who appears likely to play. “He’s not the only one across college football, or even on our team, that has shoulder pain”, Stein said. “I think everybody at this point in the year probably does, and he’s going to be ready to rock and roll. I thought he had a really good last week. Had a good day today, so looking forward to him competing.” The staff and medical team have been very cautious about getting him back into the full thing, and doing their best to get him back on the field for Saturday night in Knoxville. “It’s a balance. I do think that our trainers, our strength and conditioning, our sports science have done a really great job with CJ, and almost like that load management throughout the week, to where what does he actually need to do,” Stein said. Kentucky will need a healthy Baxter this weekend against the Vols’ No. 15 defense in the country. We’ll learn more once we receive the first availability report Wednesday evening. On Saturday, Marcus Freeman could do the same against the same program. No. 11 Notre Dame and No. 1 Miami meet in South Bend with playoff implications on the line in what is the highest-ranked matchup between the programs (according to the AP poll) since that classic Catholics vs. Convicts showdown in 1988. The Irish won the national championship that season, its most recent title. The College Football Playoff selection committee sees a different matchup. Miami sits atop the first CFP rankings, but slotted Notre Dame at No. 11, seven spots lower than the AP voters. Notre Dame is the last team in the CFP field, and a loss against Miami could knock the Irish out of playoff contention entirely. "They don't have that signature win right now," CFP committee chair Hunter Yurachek said Tuesday night on ESPN. "They've got a great opportunity in front of them at home versus Miami to get that signature win that I think they need to move up in the rankings." Don't forget, we've been here before. Miami defeated Notre Dame 27-24 in last season's season opener. The Irish remained above Miami in five CFP rankings, but the committee flipped the two in the final week, placing Miami over Notre Dame in the CFP. Miami vs. Notre Dame: Need to know Darian Mensah vs. a defense without its leader : Darian Mensah leads the FBS in completion percentage (80.7%) and pass efficiency (202.7) and is tied for the national lead with 25 touchdown passes against one interception. Notre Dame takes him on without linebacker Drayk Bowen , its leading tackler (45) and the green-dot helmet that relays defensive calls. He was ruled out with an ankle injury suffered against Navy . Malachi Toney's absence : Miami will be without superstar receiver Malachi Toney, who suffered an ankle injury in practice Wednesday and will undergo surgery in hopes of returning for the CFP. This game certainly takes on a different context. The sophomore ranks in the top three nationally in receptions (73), receiving yards per game (128.4) and receiving touchdowns (13), the last of which ties Miami's single-season school record. Cooper Barkate is the second-best receiver on the roster, but he averages 46.5 yards per game, compared to Toney's 128.4. CJ Carr's problem : Carr has been magnificent most of his career, but the splits are wild. He's thrown 18 touchdowns and one interception this season, and he is 15-0 as a starter against unranked teams. Against AP-ranked opponents, he is 2-3, completing 60.9% of his passes at 6.6 yards per attempt with six touchdowns and five interceptions. With few opportunities to impress the CFP committee, he needs to step up against the top-ranked Hurricanes. Unranked Boston College , SMU and Syracuse are the only teams remaining on the schedule. Notre Dame's invincibility : Notre Dame is 10-1 at home against Miami, and the home team has won the last eight on-campus meetings. Miami's only win at Notre Dame Stadium came in 1984. On the other side, the Hurricanes are 18-3 on the road as the AP No. 1, with all three losses at ranked teams, including the 1988 game against the Irish. Miami hasn't defeated an AP top-5 team on the road since 2005. Penalties and the red zone : Notre Dame is the most disciplined team in the FBS, averaging only 28.9 penalty yards per game. Miami ranks 82nd (58.8). The Irish defense, however, ranks 108th in red-zone defense, allowing points on 88.9% of possessions, and Miami scores on 92.9% of its own. History sides with the Irish. Now that Malachi Toney is out, siding with the Irish becomes an easy play. Notre Dame will play the nation's most efficient quarterback either way, but how different does he look without his top option? Meanwhile, Notre Dame's red-zone defense has struggled against far lesser offenses, so will Toney's absence actually matter? Miami is 5-3 against the spread this season. Notre Dame is 4-4. The Irish can win this game, but covering by five points will still be difficult. picks.blurb: Rece Davis Predicts Notre Dame Playoff Problem Ahead of Top-5 Miami Showdown Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Notre Dame could find itself in the same College Football Playoff predicament that ended its 2025 season if it can’t beat No. 1 Miami on Saturday, according to ESPN College GameDay host Rece Davis. Davis made the case on ESPN’s College GameDay Podcast with co-hosts Pete Thamel and Dan Wetzel, saying the No. 4 Fighting Irish (7-1) would be in “ very much the same situation as a year ago ” with a loss. Rece Davis on Notre Dame’s resume Notre Dame Fighting Irish head coach Marcus Freeman reacts during the first half against the Brigham Young Cougars | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Davis noted that ESPN’s Football Power Index, a forward-looking measure, ranks Notre Dame No. 1. Miami, however, ranks No. 1 in strength of record, which grades what a team has done against its schedule. Davis noted that ESPN’s Football Power Index, a forward-looking measure, ranks Notre Dame No. 1. Miami, however, ranks No. 1 in strength of record, which grades what a team has done against its schedule. Davis said that split will shape the debate over the Irish. He expects them to stay in the field unless the Hurricanes blow them out, but he doesn’t see the questions about their resume going away. “I think Notre Dame will still be OK absent getting run out of the stadium, which I cannot conceive of happening,” Davis said. “So it’s going to be a little bit different than last year, but the argument, the discussion, is going to be the same if they don’t win this game.” He added: “When you get down to who did you play and who did you beat, especially the who did you beat portion of who did you play, they won’t have much on the paper.” Why does Notre Dame’s schedule matter? General view as Brigham Young Cougars fans celebrate on the field after the game against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Notre Dame has faced one team ranked at the time of kickoff this season, and it lost 28-24 at BYU on Oct. 17. None of its seven wins came against a team in this week’s AP Top 25. Notre Dame has faced one team ranked at the time of kickoff this season, and it lost 28-24 at BYU on Oct. 17. None of its seven wins came against a team in this week’s AP Top 25. The Irish beat Wisconsin, Rice, Michigan State, Purdue, North Carolina, Stanford and Navy. After Miami, they close with Boston College, SMU and Syracuse, who are a combined 14-10 and unranked. Notre Dame does carry a protection it lacked last year. The College Football Playoff guarantees the Irish a spot if they finish in the top 12 of the final rankings. A loss to Miami would test that cushion, though, because Notre Dame would sit at 7-2 with no win over a ranked opponent and no ranked teams left on its schedule. When it comes to the gambling websites, however, it's a bit different. The odds were released for Saturday's game against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish in South Bend, Ind. According to Hard Rock Bet, the Hurricanes are a 4.5 underdog in the matchup. This should come as a surprise and it shouldn't. Despite the top ranking, the Hurricanes have shown some flaws this season. Their play on defense has been one of the issues. On Saturday, they gave up 407 yards in the 38-35 victory against the North Carolina Tar Heels. They were assisted by a late fumble recovery and the Tar Heels being twice called for a penalty on two onside kicks to avoid the upset. Despite their dominance on offense, the Hurricanes have given up at least 20 points in three games. They struggled in a 33-20 victory against the Wake Forest Demon Deacons in September. They then needed two overtimes to defeat the Florida State Seminoles in a 45-43 shootout. The Seminoles, who were a failed Hail Mary attempt from stealing a victory, amassed 433 yards. Even though the Hurricanes defeated the Pittsburgh Panthers by 29 points, they still allowed 403 yards. At some point, they need to show they can at least come up with stops should the high-powered offense have an off night. The offense, led by quarterback Darian Mensah, receiver Malachi Toney and running back Mark Fletcher, has carried UM all season. Mensah and Toney are both Heisman candidates while Fletcher just set the school record for most career touchdowns with 38. That is saying a lot considering the amount of talent that has come through Coral Gables over the years. Even though they are favored, the Fighting Irish have struggled the last two games. They had difficulty early on against the Navy Midshipmen before pulling away for a 35-13 victory on Saturday. Two weeks before, Notre Dame was upset by the BYU Cougars of the Big 12 conference. That loss now looks even worse after the Cougars followed that win with a bad loss to the UCF Knights, who were blown out Friday by the Baylor Bears. Regardless, it doesn't matter who is favored in the Miami-Notre Dame game. It is the biggest matchup of the weekend. ESPN has already dubbed it as the home for the popular College Gameday show.

This is the ND offense preview for the week. The 'Canes are 5th overall in SP+ while ND is 3rd . The Irish kicking game is 17th while UM's is ranked 19th . Per ESPN , ND has a 61.3 % win expectancy as 4.5 point favorites at home. The Irish are 3rd in FBS in scoring offense putting up 40.4 PPG which is 2nd to only Miami and North Texas. The ND offense is 2nd in SP+ offense behind only the Miami Hurricanes. The high scoring Irish offense will be up against Miami's defense which is 23rd now in SP+ after the UNC game. The 'Canes are 25th in scoring allowed while giving up 19.3 PPG. The Irish are 36th in FBS in 3rd down conversion offense, picking up the 1st 43 % of the time. On 4th down ND is 16th in FBS picking up the 1st 74 % of the time. Miami's 3rd down defense is 95th in FBS allowing opponents to move the sticks 42 % of the time. ND's turnover margin per game is 3rd in FBS at +1.8 while Miami is 9th at +1.0 TOMPG. For obvious reasons I'm looking at ND's lone loss to BYU and their win over UNC. ND lost to BYU 28-24 and beat UNC 37-26 . Against UNC the Irish offense finished 7-of-16 on money downs with zero turnovers. CJ Carr averaged 8.1 yards per pass attempt with five total TD's against the Tar Heels. The Irish averaged 5.4 yards per carry while Jordan Faison caught two TD's on 16.5 yards per catch. UNC finished with zero sacks, two TFL's and five PBU's versus the Irish offense. Above- Splitting two lost safeties with a deep post… gives me some nervous vibes here re the ND receivers and CJ Carr carving up the Miami safety room with a deep shot. Above- More abuse on safety types with a slot fade. One of my favorite passing concepts. If he's even, he's leavin' and he'll head to the front pylon here. Above- ND ran a little wide zone, the RB bounces this one outside and takes advantage of the UNC DB's in the open field. Miami is really struggling in the open field without Keionte Scott. Above- UNC gets caught here with both DB's to that side being aggressive and playing down on the short throw. Miami is more likely to have both on the deep shot and no one short. I don't see this being as much of an issue with the 'Canes in country cover 3. Above- The check down to the RB's in the middle of the field is a Miami weakness. Toure and Smith need to play tighter coverage and rally to help each other at the ball. Above- Keep CJ Carr inside. Here UNC plays an outside contain on QB sweep and it forces Carr inside for a loss. Staying on that outside hip is key. Above- ND can fight for the tough yards. Here they pick up 4th and 2 on the inside and in a me vs you rep ND's RB wins. Above- An explosive TFL from an edge guy squeeze and chasing from the back side? I like Marquise Lightfoot here for this type of havoc play. Let him chase this down and not drop into the flats, please. Above- The UNC player has to fight to get outside of CJ Carr's right hip. If he can get out there he can box the Q back to his help. Instead Carr gets outside and scrambles for a TD. He can and will run vs. Miami's slow LB's. Above- An open field shot with the sideline there for help… and it's missed? Looks really familiar to me from the Miami defense. Miami has to clean up open field angles and tackling vs. ND. Against BYU the Irish offense finished 12-of-23 on money downs with one turnover. Carr averaged only 5.3 yards per attempt with zero TD's and a lost fumble. The Cougars didn't sack Carr but picked up three TFL's and seven PBU's. Jaden Greathouse led the way for ND with 15.6 yards per catch while the rushing attack was held to 3.8 yards per carry but had two scores. Above- James is going to be a tough one to take down. He had BYU lunging all over the place as he juked and cut for 4.8 yards per carry vs. a top-25 SP+ defense. Above- How do you blow up counter? BYU doesn't wrong arm it but they do control the edge, they also get interior penetration. This is a MUST HAVE game from Moten and Scott at DT. Above- Even in blanket coverage ND has been getting work from Faison, Greathouse and Bettis Jr. on the outside to name a few. That's hardly Miami's flaccid zone. Above- James with another shifty carry. He's a one-cut-and-go back like Mallory. Above- The ND OL dominated BYU's front 6 here and gave the back two ways to go in the red zone. He used his eyes, saw where the safety wasn't, and scored. Above- CJ Carr has aded the dreaded back shoulder throw to his repertoire and the ND WR's can get a little fyzical. That's not great, Bob, for a CB crew that looks baby dookie soft. Above- Carr has always been a solid scrambler, he's really improved at that skill this season. He scrambled around to find a wide open target here and Miami can't let WR's get behind them on scramble drill plays. Above- This is where Smith and Toure should excel, except teams have baited them inside and thrown some RPO's that have them stick. Damned if you do, damned if you don't. It's why a lot of LB coaches are now using a squat technique where the LB doesn't take 2-read steps forward, instead he hits a quick baby squat to force the run on 2nd level RPO's. Above- Hetherman has cut Toure off at what he does best- run blitz. Where are those TFL run throughs from a year ago? Get the AARPLB out of pass drops and let him blitz. Above- Pretty crazy not to call DPI on this slot fade but ND did get away with the throw-by on the back shoulder throw earlier. Just a tough call (also this was another clock disaster, right?) for the win. The Canyonero Keys to Victory main theme from the summer was that Miami needs to win bully ball vs. Notre Dame. I'm not so sure if that's true now after the season has unfolded the way it has. Miami may now have to win a shoot out vs. ND and CJ Carr. The 'Canes pass defense is horrendous and ND clearly saw the UNC game on film and will try to attack the outside with WR's vs Safeties and the inside with TE's deep up the seam. Miami needs to improve their tackling, and coverage when it comes to the safety position. The LB's are a lost cause in space. Miami will continue to see screens, seams, digs, and outs until the CB's prove they'll tackle, and the LB/S prove they'll cover. We'll get to the individual keys in the ND Defense preview that's out Friday at 8am.

The Hurricanes are No. 1 in the AP Top 25 poll as well, but will be an underdog when they go to South Bend to take on the Fighting Irish this weekend. According to Yahoo Sports research, it appears to be the first time that a team ranked No. 1 in the CFP is an underdog against a team ranked outside of the top 10. The Fighting Irish are ranked fourth in the AP poll. Notre Dame was up to a 6.5-point favorite at some sportsbooks on Thursday afternoon, but that number has moved all the way out to -8.5 because of the news that star Miami WR Malachi Toney needs ankle surgery and will miss the game . The line opened at -4.5 and had moved the Fighting Irish's direction despite the bulk of the early betting action on the Hurricanes at some books. "We're seeing two-way action, taking more money on Notre Dame spread and the Miami moneyline," Joey Feazel, lead college football trader at Caesars Sportsbook, told Yahoo Sports. Number feels right to me." Hurricanes QB Darian Mensah and Ohio State WR Jeremiah Smith are now Heisman co-favorites at +150. Notre Dame QB CJ Carr has the third-best odds at +600, so there will plenty of movement in the Heisman market depending on how this game turns out. Toney moved from +325 to off the board. away.headline: Miami gets concerning Malachi Toney injury update ahead of Notre Dame clash
away.blurb: Miami will undoubtedly want Toney available for this crucial matchup, but playing through an ankle injury could bring risks for one of the Hurricanes’ most valuable offensive weapons. The undefeated Miami Hurricanes face a major test this weekend when they battle the Notre Dame Fighting Irish in a showdown between College Football Playoff contenders. Miami enters the matchup ranked No. 1 in both the AP Top 25 poll and the initial CFP rankings. Much of that has been thanks to the on-field brilliance of quarterback Darian Mensah and star wide receiver Malachi Toney. However, a concerning injury update regarding Toney surfaced on Wednesday, potentially putting his availability for the Notre Dame matchup in jeopardy. According to ESPN’s Pete Thamel , sources told him and Max Olson that the Hurricanes’ Toney is dealing with an ankle injury, leaving his status for Saturday’s matchup “uncertain.” “Toney is expected to press and attempt to play, given the magnitude of the game,” Thamel also said in his X report. More news: CFP Committee Chair Under Fire for Alabama’s Controversial Ranking Toney ranks second in NCAA football with 73 receptions, third with 1,027 receiving yards, and third with 13 touchdowns. The 5-foot-11 sophomore has delivered several impressive performances this past season, including 154 yards and two touchdowns in Miami’s double-overtime win over Florida State. As of this writing, Toney is also considered one of the leading Heisman Trophy contenders. Mensah has emerged as the favorite to win, and Toney’s production has played a significant role in the quarterback’s success this season. Saturday’s game carries major CFP implications for Miami and Notre Dame. Both teams appeared in the initial CFP rankings, with Miami holding the top spot and Notre Dame landing at No. 11. However, several games remain on their schedules before the playoff field is finalized. A loss could seriously damage Notre Dame’s chances of getting into the College Football Playoff. The undefeated Miami Hurricanes face a major test this weekend when they battle the Notre Dame Fighting Irish in a showdown between College Football Playoff contenders. According to ESPN’s Pete Thamel , sources told him and Max Olson that the Hurricanes’ Toney is dealing with an ankle injury, leaving his status for Saturday’s matchup “uncertain.” “Toney is expected to press and attempt to play, given the magnitude of the game,” Thamel also said in his X report. As of this writing, Toney is also considered one of the leading Heisman Trophy contenders. Mensah has emerged as the favorite to win, and Toney’s production has played a significant role in the quarterback’s success this season. Saturday’s game carries major CFP implications for Miami and Notre Dame. Both teams appeared in the initial CFP rankings, with Miami holding the top spot and Notre Dame landing at No. 11. home.headline: Why Bill O’Brien Hopes Boston College Captain Michael Crounse Returns Against Notre Dame
home.blurb: CHESTNUT HILL, Mass. — The morning after Boston College football’s initial student-athlete availability report for Saturday’s contest against FSU came out, head coach Bill O’Brien spoke on the injury designation for Michael Crounse, the Eagles’ starting center and a prized team captain. The impact Crounse has for BC is paramount for a variety of reasons — that could be seen when he made his return from injury against Georgia Tech in Week 8 , as the Eagles ran for nearly 400 yards. But in BC’s Week 9 loss on the road to Duke , his lower leg got rolled on quite badly in the second half, which forced him out of the game and into a boot. “I mean, he’s progressing,” said O’Brien. “He was in a boot. He’s out of the boot already. So we’ll see for Notre Dame. [I] really, really want him to play against Notre Dame.” While Crounse is officially out this week, the Eagles’ road contest in South Bend, Ind., next week against the Fighting Irish will be a particularly special one for the redshirt junior. Boston College Football Tight End Kaelan Chudzinski Confirmed Available for Duke Game But the main reason that he makes such a big difference on the field stems from his veteran presence in the huddle, which is undeniably a key trait in all levels of sport, especially football. After suffering a knee injury in the Eagles’ Week 1 loss at Cincinnati, Crounse missed four straight games before returning against the Yellow Jackets, and he finished that game without any major setbacks. O’Brien technically confirmed it isn’t a season-ending injury, which is positive news for the Eagles. But it will at least sideline him for this week’s matchup, and possibly one that has been marked on Crounse’s calendar for months. That is because Crounse’s father, Mike, played for Notre Dame from 1986-90, highlighted by a consensus national championship in an undefeated 12-0 1988 season. “It’s a special game for him,” O’Brien said. “But there’s not much we can do about it. We feel terrible for Mike, but it is what it is.” Freshman DJ Williams, who has a 48.7 offensive grade on PFF (Pro Football Focus), which ranks near the very bottom of FBS centers that qualify for a grade, will be making his fifth-career start in Crounse’s place. It is not an ideal situation to be thrust into as an underclassmen, especially as a replacement for a captain of all people. But Williams now has enough experience under his belt to enter Saturday’s showdown with the Seminoles carrying a bit more confidence than he had at the beginning of the season, when he was essentially tossed straight into the ring of fire with no legitimate playing time to lean on as a guidance tool. “DJ’s got another opportunity,” O’Brien said. “And DJ’s had a good week. DJ’s a great dude, and he’s a really good guy who’s practiced very well.” Follow us on Twitter/X , Facebook , YouTube , Instagram , and Tiktok for the latest Boston College news. Plus, a loss here would be their third in SEC play, essentially ending their conference title hopes, and putting them in a position where they need to win out and hope for some other teams to lose to return to the playoff. Georgia vs. Ole Miss: Need to know This is the fifth straight time these two have met while ranked: Maybe that doesn't seem like something that's all that impressive to you, but for context, it had happened only five times in the first 46 meetings between the schools. Georgia has had the better end of most meetings, as they lead the series 34-14-1, and a win for Ole Miss this weekend would give the Rebels consecutive wins over the Dawgs for the first time since the 1995 and 1996 seasons. Kirby Smart has done well against ranked opponents: The Georgia coach is 44-18 against AP-ranked teams during his tenure in Athens. That's the fifth-best record by any head coach against ranked teams in AP Poll history (minimum of 20 games). That includes a stretch of six wins in their last seven against ranked teams. The last loss? To Ole Miss in the playoff last year. Trinidad Chambliss could tie a school record here: Chambliss has thrown for at least one touchdown in 21 consecutive games. If he throws one against Georgia, it will put him in a tie with former Ole Miss QB Chad Kelly for most consecutive games with a TD pass at 22. This game is going to be a massive one for the SEC standings, because the Bulldogs have a wide-open pathway to making the SEC Championship Game, while the Rebels are fighting to stay alive. I'm giving the edge to the Rebels, given that the game is in Oxford, and the two losses for Ole Miss came on the road. Ole Miss should have some success moving the football, and Chambliss will give the Bulldogs' defense a few uncomfortable moments. However, I have some concerns about whether the Rebels can consistently get enough stops against Georgia's offense. Gunner Stockton doesn't need to put together a spectacular performance for Georgia to win this game. I expect him to be nearly flawless, making smart decisions, taking what the defense gives him, and avoiding the costly mistakes that could swing momentum. The Bulldogs should be able to control the game offensively and take advantage of an Ole Miss defense that struggles to get off the field. Chambliss keeps the Rebels within striking distance for a while, but Georgia's balance and execution ultimately prove too much. – Ryan Roberts , A to Z Notre Dame Ole Miss 24, Georgia 21 We need another Heisman moment from Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss, and I'm guessing we will see it. Ole Miss offense needs to step up big, and we will see them do just that. picks.headline: Georgia football coach Kirby Smart previews Ole Miss game
picks.blurb: Georgia football coach Kirby Smart previews Ole Miss game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Georgia football coach Kirby Smart previews Ole Miss game Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Georgia Bulldogs head coach Kirby Smart heavily praised Ole Miss Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss during his weekly press conference. Smart is quite familiar with Chambliss and Ole Miss . Georgia played Chambliss twice last year including in the Sugar Bowl, which the Rebels won 39-34. Georgia won the regular season meeting in Athens, 43-35. Georgia (7-1, 5-1 SEC) and Ole Miss (6-2, 4-2 SEC) are both in the thick of the SEC championship and College Football Playoff hunt. The winner on Saturday night (7:30 p.m. ET on Nov. 7) will find themselves in a much better position while the losers will find themselves much worse off. Specifically, Ole Miss could be facing playoff elimination with a loss to Georgia since the Rebels have an ugly blowout loss to Florida. We're likely looking at another high-stakes shootout between Georgia and Ole Miss. Here's what Georgia coach Kirby Smart said about Ole Miss with most of the media's questions focusing on Chambliss. Smart's opening statement on Ole Miss "It's on to Ole Miss, a really good football team," Smart said at his weekly press conference. "Pete (Golding) has done a tremendous job since taking over. "Obviously, we know the two games last year with them were both really hard-fought battles, hard games, a lot of ebb-and-flow in both games. They've done a tremendous job this year. They probably have the best quarterback in the country who plays at a high level. He is extremely hard to defend and a great player. "I have a lot of respect for their staff. I know a lot of those guys and the team, the way their team competes and plays. They're playing really well right now. At home, they've been exceptionally well. Our guys will be excited for the challenge. Another opportunity. Another week in the SEC, as it always is. It'll be a great atmosphere." On how to defend Chambliss Mississippi Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (6) passes the ball against the Louisiana State Tigers "How long do you have?" Smart said. "We could talk for an hour about it, but it's not even that. "I wrote down, so I watched every game, wow plays. It's not the wow plays. The wow plays are what you guys love and what America loves. He had some wow plays against us last year in both games, but especially the second. "It's the down-in, down-out decision making that he's really elite at. The accuracy that he's elite at, the release, the decision. His pinpointing. He has an anticipation of windows that's probably unmatched. I don't know if that was God-given or the fact that he played a lot of football before he got to Ole Miss. He has played a lot of football and experience helps. "You throw all that in, and you have a tremendous athlete. He goes forwards, backwards as fast as he goes sideways. He can back up and go for it. He's just a great athlete that is a great quarterback." On Chambliss' pre-snap and post-snap ability "I can't get inside his head and say what he's doing pre-snap, post-snap," Smart adds. "He's elite at both, in my opinion. He surveys the field. He knows what he's going to do. He's been in this offense long enough that he knows what he's basing his decisions on, and then after the play's snapped, he goes through his progressions and does a great job. "He knows how to navigate a pocket. I think his pocket presence people don't give him enough credit for it. This guy's not just like a take-off-and-run guy. He steps up in the pocket. He goes through the pocket. He's made some of his best 'wow' plays working through the pocket." On Ole Miss' red zone success "You have to play well in the red zone," Smart said. "A lot of that has to do with the quarterback extending plays and running the game. The quarterback run game in the red area really shows up with every team. He's a tremendous decision maker in terms of what he wants to do with the ball. "There's two, three plays in the red area this year that you would say, 'He's never even supposed to pull that ball.' He does it and makes huge plays. He's doing that against SEC teams. That makes him hard to defend in the red area. They got really good skill players, and he's got really good touch and accuracy to make throws. All those things combined to be a good red zone player. "It's hard to say, 'What do you do in the red zone?' You have to play well. You have to play disciplined football, and you have to make it hard to run it in on. That's what most people that are good in the red zone can do." On containing Chambliss and the Ole Miss offense "You have to be successful at a lot of things," Smart notes. "You have to be able to pitch and catch, not just do one thing. There's nothing we're going to do that he hadn't seen. You're not tricking the guy. I think that's what people get infatuated with, is, 'How can I trick him and do that?' You can't do that. "You have to go play good sound football. You have tackle the man that catches it. No yard after catch. You have to create some turnover. You have to bat some balls. You have to make plays and get off the field when you have a chance on third down. There's not a perfect remedy. If there was, somebody would have done it." Follow UGA Wire on Instagram , Facebook , X (formerly Twitter) or Threads for more Georgia football coverage! I’ve just got to keep that in the back of my head burning.” Georgia (7-1, 5-1 SEC) is No. 2 in the first CFP rankings so it won’t be knocked out of the national title chase with a loss in Saturday night's game in Oxford, Miss., but it could do serious damage to Ole Miss (6-2, 4-2) which is No. 10. “We’ve got two losses,” Ole Miss defensive tackle Will Echoles said. “Right now, it’s to the point where every game we play is a playoff game that we’ve got to win. That’s the mindset we’ve got.” Georgia vs. Ole Miss predictions This isn’t the same Georgia defense that Chambliss had big games against last year. The Bulldogs have recorded 26 sacks, 6 more than it had all of last season. Georgia didn’t record one sack against Chambliss last year in two games, including a 43-35 Bulldog win in Athens. That’s with Chambliss throwing 82 passes combined. “We’ve just got to keep him in the trap,” Griffin said. “We can’t let him escape. Obviously, he’s a great escape artist. He’s fast, he’s capable of doing anything. A great quarterback, has great vision.” Ole Miss has given up only five sacks. “Just knowing that he’ll use his legs to create plays and knowing we have to rush as a unit up front and give him different looks in the secondary that he’ll be uncomfortable with,” outside linebacker Quintavius Johnson said. Chambliss was 30 of 46 for 362 yards and 2 touchdowns in the Sugar Bowl and 19 of 36 for 263 with a touchdown and two rushing touchdowns in the regular season Georgia win. He's passed for 2,189 yards with 18 touchdowns and 8 interceptions this season while completing 63.9% of his passes. “He had some wow plays against us last year,” Georgia coach Kirby Smart said. “Really in both games, but especially the second. But It's the down-in, down-out decision-making that he's really elite at, the accuracy that he's elite at. The release, the decision. He's just pinpoint. He has an anticipation of windows that's probably unmatched.” Deuce Alexander and Horatio Fields are Chambliss’ top targets. Alexander has 48 catches for 669 receiving yards and 5 touchdowns, but has had drops lately. Georgia needs Ellis Robinson to be his usual self or Braylon Conley to step up if Robinson is affected by an apparent knee injury sustained during Florida game. Georgia vs. Ole Miss scouting report Why Georgia has an advantage: The Sugar Bowl loss will be motivation for some players and the Bulldogs' domination of Florida made the Auburn loss look like a strange outlier for Georgia's body of work this season. Georgia already won in a tough road environment at Alabama at night. Why Ole Miss has an advantage: Chambliss is one of the most dynamic players in college football as Georgia saw firsthand in two games last season. The Rebels are hard to beat at home. It has won 16 straight at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, the second longest streak in FBS behind Ohio's 17. Georgia vs. Ole Miss injury updates Georgia: WR Isiah Canion (lower extremity, probable), RB Chauncey Bowens (lower body, questionable), WR Thomas Blackshear (collarbone, questionable), TE Elyiss Williams (undisclosed, questionable), DT Joseph Jonah-Ajonye (undisclosed, questionable), DB Tyriq Green (leg, questionable), LB AJ Kruah (undisclosed, questionable) RB Dante Dowdell (multiple injuries including collarbone, lung and arm, out), OLB Amaris Williams (knee, out). Ole Miss: RB Kewan Lacy (shoulder, out), CB Jalyn Crawford (shoulder, probable), LB Kam Franklin (undisclosed, out), LB Keaton Thomas (undisclosed, out), WR Izaiah Hartrup (undisclosed, out), CB Cedrick Beavers (undisclosed, probable), S Edwin Joseph (undisclosed, out), S MJ Preston (undisclosed, probable), LB Ant Davis (undisclosed, out), WR Kevin Johnson (undisclosed out), S Nascar McCoy (undisclosed, out), S Gerald Lacy (undisclosed, out), OL Carius Curne (undisclosed, out), WR Samari Reed (undisclosed, out), OL Terez Davis (undisclosed, out) Georgia 31, Ole Miss 27: The matchup of Ole Miss's SEC top scoring offense in league games against Georgia's No. 1 scoring defense should be get out your popcorn stuff. Even with Trinidad Chambliss, I trust Georgia to win that battle and get enough plays from Gunner Stockton and the running game to escape Oxford with the victory. That's more that he did not convert than each of the last two seasons when he went 17 of 19 in 2025 and 21 of 23 in 2024. The misses have been from 43 yards, 54 and 39. Ole Miss' Lucas Carneiro is 12 of 15 with a long of 57. Ole Miss defensive back Joenel Aguero: The senior started as the Star position for Georgia against the Rebels last year in Athens, but lost his starting job to Rasean Dinkins late in the season and transferred. The Rebels' starter is a physical tackler, but Georgia could target him in the passing game. He started 12 games last season with 39 tackles and an interception. He has 27 tackles and a pass breakup this season. Composure of Georgia offensive line: The Bulldogs already went into a high-profile environment on the road this season and won at Alabama. How will Georgia handle another raucous environment in another night game after the offense didn't make many plays downfield against Florida? Communication will be key to avoid costly false start penalties. Ole Miss DT Will Echoles: The 6-foot-3, 315-pound junior had two tackles for loss, five tackles and two pass breakups in the Sugar Bowl win over Georgia last season. Georgia will need to contain him. Gunner Stockton had several passes batted down against Florida and keeping Echoles out of passing lanes and out of the backfield will be key. He has 21 tackles, 4 tackles for loss and 1 1/2 sacks this season. Bold predictions for Georgia football vs Ole Miss Gunner Stockton makes plays downfield: Georgia won handedly against Florida behind 217 rushing yards and didn't need to do much in the passing game after opening a 24-0 halftime lead and with the defense forcing Florida turnovers. That shouldn't be the case against an Ole Miss offense that can be explosive. Georgia has shown it can make plays downfield and Stockton will take more shots and hit his share. Ball security will continue to be an issue: Kirby Smart pushed back when asked after the Florida win about another Sacovie-White Helton muff on a punt return, but Georgia has four this season and has fumbled 14 times, which ranks 126th in the nation, according to ESPN's Bill Connelly. Georgia is fortunate to only have lost 5 fumbles this season, but the Bulldogs are living dangerously. Georgia defensive line will push the pocket : One difference between this Georgia defense and last year is that it's getting to the quarterback more by pushing the pocket which could put pressure on Chambliss. Georgia has 7 1/2 sacks from interior defensive linemen including two each from Elijah Griffin, Josh Horton and Anthony Lonon. It had just 3 1/2 last season. Run game gets cranked up: Georgia has rushed for an average of 225.7 yards per game in its four games away from Athens. The Rebels have looked vulnerable against the run at times this season. It ranks 76th in the nation, allowing 148.9 per game. Texas kept the ball on the ground during an 80-yard drive for a go-ahead touchdown in beating Ole Miss.

away.headline: Ole Miss vs. Georgia injury report: Kewan Lacy out, Luke Ferrelli in
away.blurb: The first Ole Miss availability report for Georgia landed Wednesday, and like most injury reports this time of year, it came with a little bit of everything. Let's start with the good news. Linebacker Luke Ferrelli wasn't listed at all. Considering where things stood a week ago, that's a significant development. Ferrelli has been battling an ankle injury for weeks and spent all of last week on the report after aggravating it in practice. He started against Auburn but was limited before leaving the game early. His absence from Wednesday's report is about as positive a sign as Ole Miss could have hoped for heading into Saturday's showdown with No. 2 Georgia. Now for the bad news. Running back Kewan Lacy and safety Edwin Joseph are both out. Lacy's status was expected . Ole Miss has been preparing as if it would be without its star running back, so there were no surprises there. Joseph's designation is a little tougher to swallow. There was at least a sliver of hope he could return after missing four straight games following ankle surgery, but that won't happen this week. The rest of the report falls somewhere in the middle. Defensive lineman Kam Franklin and leading tackler Keaton Thomas were listed as questionable, while cornerback Jalyn Crawford and left tackle Terez Davis were listed as probable. None of those designations are expected to keep them off the field Saturday. Ole Miss has been preparing as if it would be without its star running back, so there were no surprises there. Joseph's designation is a little tougher to swallow. There was at least a sliver of hope he could return after missing four straight games following ankle surgery, but that won't happen this week. The rest of the report falls somewhere in the middle. Defensive lineman Kam Franklin and leading tackler Keaton Thomas were listed as questionable, while cornerback Jalyn Crawford and left tackle Terez Davis were listed as probable. None of those designations are expected to keep them off the field Saturday. home.blurb: So far this season, Lacy has had 421 yards and five touchdowns in 88 touches. He's building off of a breakout sophomore season, where he registered 1,567 yards and 24 touchdowns on 306 carries. He played twice against Georgia, recording 31 yards and two touchdowns on 12 carries in the regular-season loss and another 98 yards and two touchdowns on 22 carries in Ole Miss's Sugar Bowl win. Georgia fans will keep his status in mind this weekend. The SEC availability report comes out on Wednesday night. No. 2 Georgia (7-1, 5-1 in SEC) goes on the road to face No. 12 Ole Miss (6-2, 4-2 in SEC) in Oxford. Lacy missed the Rebels' 45-15 win against Auburn on Oct. 31. Golding said Lacy is still recovering and rehabbing from the injury. "It's a work in progress," Golding said. "We're not expecting to have him this week. This isn't something that's going to happen overnight. He's still working hard at it. Hopefully we'll know sooner than later, but not expecting him this week."
