Shekai Mills-Knight led the team with 71 rushing yards in 16 carries, and JT Lindsey also got three carries. Lacy injured the same shoulder in Ole Miss' win against LSU, and it caused him to miss the game against Florida. He first injured that shoulder in last year's College Football Playoff win over Tulane. While he stayed active during the rest of Ole Miss's run to the CFP semifinal, he underwent offseason surgery. picks.headline: Florida Gets Strong Prediction Heading Into Oklahoma Showdown
picks.blurb: Florida Gets Strong Prediction Heading Into Oklahoma Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Florida Gets Strong Prediction Heading Into Oklahoma Showdown (Scott Wachter-Imagn Images) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 4, 2026 at 9:23 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads As the Florida Gators get ready for their upcoming SEC game against the Oklahoma Sooners, the team will have to figure out a way to bounce back. Florida was blown out a week ago by the Georgia Bulldogs, seeing them drop their third game of the season. But the Gators have been a resilient group all year long, and this team will be asked to make it happen again. Entering the game, the Gators hold a record of 5-3 on the year, with the team going 3-3 so far in SEC games. Florida is ranked at No. 23 for the week, staying alive in the first edition of the College Football Playoff rankings. As for the Sooners, they will be coming into the game with a record of 4-4 for the year, going 2-3 in SEC play so far. This team has underperformed this season, but the Gators can't overlook them at all. Oklahoma still has star quarterback John Mateer under center, and he can do damage against this Gators defense. Florida is going to have to be very careful in the game, looking to avoid being upset at home. As the two teams prepare for the SEC battle, the Gators are being favored to come away with the win this week. Florida has been given a 64 percent chance to take down Oklahoma at home, according to the ESPN matchup predictor . One way for the Gators to get an edge in the game is to get running back Jadan Baugh back into a strong rhythm. After an incredible start to the season, the star back has slowed down heavily, with him going 100 yards on the ground for four straight games. Baugh still has put together a special season for Florida, with him rushing for 801 yards with 13 touchdowns. But when the Gators are at their best, Baugh is going up and down the field, opening the offense up. If Florida is able to get Baugh going again this week, it could help the offense out, giving the team a much stronger chance to take down the Sooners. Oklahoma can have an explosive offensive attack, so the Gators may be forced to put up points in order to keep up with them. Kickoff for this game between the Gators and the Sooners is scheduled for 4:45 p.m. PT/7:45 p.m. ET from Ben Hill Griffin Stadium in Gainesville.

picks.headline: Florida Given Favorable Odds to Defeat Oklahoma in Week 10
picks.blurb: Florida Given Favorable Odds to Defeat Oklahoma in Week 10 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB March Madness TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Florida Given Favorable Odds to Defeat Oklahoma in Week 10 (IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect) Jordon Lawrenz · Roundtable Sports Mon, November 2, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Not only did the spread for the Florida Gators vs. Oklahoma Sooners open at four-points, but it later moved two-points further in the Gators favor. Head coach Jon Sumrall let his thoughts be heard after a brutal loss in Atlanta, but at the end of the day there's no shame in losing to the now No. 2-ranked Georgia Bulldogs. Still, dropping a third game this year stung quite a bit, and Florida had far too many things work against them in that game. Most of their wounds were self inflicted, so that's a major focal point heading into Week 10 when Oklahoma comes to town. The Sooners are just 2-3 in conference play, and they're now six-point underdogs, according to DraftKings , ahead of this matchup on Saturday, Nov. 7. At the time of writing, the money line is set at -205 for Florida, meaning a $205 bet would win $100 in return. No one is anticipating that this game will be a blowout, nor should they be as Florida has a bad home loss this year to South Carolina. That Ole Miss win was quickly forgotten about after the Gators were embarrassed on the road at Missouri, and then back at home against the Gamecocks. Remember, this is the same Oklahoma team that beat Texas a few weeks ago, so while it's an impressive feat for Florida to have, the Sooners are in the same conversation. Oklahoma is +170 in the money line, so a $100 bet would net $170 should the Sooners prevail. The over-under is currently set at 47.5 points, though that seems low with how these defenses have played this season. As always, the spread, over-under, and money line will fluctuate throughout the week, though it was quite notable to see Florida jump to six-point favorites after it only opened as a four-point spread. To say there's a quarterback controversy in Gainesville would be an understatement. Aaron Philo looked horrendous in Atlanta, so it's safe to assume that Tramell Jones Jr. will be the Week 10 starter. Oklahoma has John Mateer leading the way, and he's meant everything to a Sooners team that has just 854 rushing yards as a team. For reference, Jadan Baugh has 801 himself, so that's one of the clear areas where the Gators should have an advantage, at least on paper, going into this one.

picks.headline: Florida vs. Oklahoma Final Score Predictions: Experts predict fascinating battle between two traditional powers with QB issues
picks.blurb: Florida vs. Oklahoma Final Score Predictions: Experts predict fascinating battle between two traditional powers with QB issues - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Scott Wachter-Imagn Images, BRYAN TERRY/THE OKLAHOMAN-Imagn Images Brandon Little, Craig Smith, Justin Churchill, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness · AtoZ Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Florida Gators and Oklahoma Sooners meet for the first time in SEC play, and both teams have questions at quarterback. The Florida Gators and Oklahoma Sooners are set to meet for just the third time in history on Saturday night, and it will be the first game in The Swamp. In the history of both programs, they have met twice: 2008 BCS National Championship Game (Florida won 24- 14) and 2020 Cotton Bowl (Oklahoma won 55-20). This year, it will be a much different game than both before it, as both quarterback spots are in a tough spot. The Gators have a quarterback controversy with Aaron Philo and Tramell Jones Jr., while Oklahoma has had numerous issues with John Mateer, leading to the dismissal of offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle. Who will get the win and take one step forward? It's primed to be a great game, and our experts predicted the game. Florida 20, Oklahoma 9 It was disappointing to see the Gators fail to take advantage of their impressive defensive performance against the Georgia Bulldogs, but it was two consecutive plus performances for a unit that has been rough this season. Now you give that unit John Mateer with Jason Witten calling plays for the first time? This could be a disaster for the Sooners. – Tyler Forness , A to Z Florida Florida 34, Oklahoma 13 Florida likely saw their playoff hopes extinguished last weekend against Georgia, but they've got a golden opportunity to get right on Saturday at home against Oklahoma. The Sooners fired offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle after a blowout home loss to South Carolina, and there's no reason to believe that things are going to improve on the road against a Gators defense that held Georgia relatively in check offensively last week. Jadan Baugh and the Gators get things rolling early, and Oklahoma lacks the horses to keep this a game by mid-third quarter. – Craig Smith , A to Z Miami Florida 21, Oklahoma 10 This game is going to be a grind, with neither offense finding much consistency throughout the afternoon. Oklahoma's defense will do its part to keep the Sooners in it, making life difficult for the Gators and keeping the score within one possession for much of the game. But John Mateer and the Oklahoma offense continue to look like a major problem. The Sooners struggle to sustain drives, miss opportunities and put too much pressure on their defense to carry the load. Florida won't exactly light up the scoreboard either, but the Gators will do enough to eventually pull away. Their defense should take advantage of Oklahoma's offensive struggles, while the offense finds just enough success to put points on the board. The game stays uncomfortably close into the fourth quarter before Florida puts together a late scoring drive to finally seal it. It won't be pretty, but the Gators will take it. Florida wins 21-10. – Ryan Roberts , A to Z Notre Dame Florida 27, Oklahoma 20 This game features two teams on opposite ends of the preseason spectrum. Yes, the Gators have 3 losses heading into November, but they have some of the best wins in the conference after beating Ole Miss and Texas. The Gators look to be in good hands with Jon Sumrall for years to come, as he has exceeded all year-one expectations. For OU, things couldn't have gone more wrong. John Mateer regressed, the offense has been horrific, and OC Ben Arbuckle was just let go this week. Still, the defense and Brent Venables will create trouble for a Florida Gators offense that can look like one of the best in the country one week, and a mess the next. But catching the Sooners in the swamp will be a win for Florida. I expect Jadan Baugh and the defense to do enough to prevent the new OC bump for the Sooners. – Rob Gregson , A to Z Alabama Florida 23, Oklahoma 17 Florida is coming off a blowout loss to Georgia that'll have them wanting to get right at home. Oklahoma making staff changes could result in some early juice from the Sooners' offense, as we sometimes see with programs after a big change. However, I think the Gators are going to move to 6-3 and keep alive what has been a solid first season for Jon Sumrall in Gainesville. The QB situation is going to matter against a talented Oklahoma defense, but the Gators will figure it out. – Brandon Little , A to Z Ohio State Final Prediction for Florida vs. Oklahoma To nobody's surprise, our experts are in favor of the Gators here. The Sooners are in a really tough spot, and a trip to The Swamp with a first-time play caller isn't likely to help any. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. away.headline: How Oklahoma State Could Deal with Tate Romney, Jaleel Johnson Injuries
away.blurb: The veterans came out of Saturday’s game with Iowa State dealing with injuries. Head coach Eric Morris told reporters on Tuesday that Oklahoma State was hopeful that both could play this week. Johnson is in his fifth season with the Cowboys and has 16 tackles and two sacks. He missed several games last year with an injury and was named a starter coming out of fall camp. He had his arm in a sling late in the game at Iowa State. Morris essentially ruled out tight end Carson Kolb on Tuesday. The redshirt sophomore, who suffered an injury to his left foot against Colorado, did not play against Iowa State. Morris said it “wouldn’t be this weekend” for Kolb’s return and that he would probably need a week or two more. Oklahoma State Designates Carson Kolb as Out for Iowa State Game The Oklahoma State Cowboys will be tracking the statuses of both linebacker Tate Romney and defensive end Jaleel Johnson this week. That means it’s likely that the pair will be on the Cowboys ’ player availability report all week – and that they’ll need to make sure they have a backup plan in case one or both are unable to play against the Kansas State Wildcats on Saturday. Replacing Tate Romney and Jaleel Johnson Romney has been Oklahoma State’s starter at MIKE linebacker all season and has already tallied a career-best 61 tackles with 1.5 sacks and a forced fumble. He previously had 52 tackles in 2023 with Arizona State. He finished the Iowa State game with nine tackles. OSU could go a couple of different directions if he cannot play. His direct backup on the depth chart is Taurean Davis, who has not started a game this year and had only one tackle this season. The Cowboys would more likely turn to Isaiah Chisom, who is listed as the starter at will linebacker but doesn’t start due to OSU’s 4-2-5 alignment. But he has 42 tackles alongside Romney and SAM linebacker Ethan Wesloski. Safety Quinton Hammonds had his arm in a sling in the later stages of the Colorado game but played against Iowa State. It’s not clear how serious Johnson’s injury is or if it’s similar. Malik Charles could start if Johnson cannot go. He has seen significant playing time as a backup and has 15 tackles and 3.5 sacks, along with an interception. Keviyan Huddleston started the only game that Johnson did not and is similar in body type. He could draw his second start of the year, based on the matchup. Huddleston has 17 tackles and a sack. Without him, Oscar Hammond received most of the snaps at tight end against Cyclones as he caught one pass. Hammond was at North Texas last year but didn’t play due to an injury. Morris did call Hammond the team’s best downfield threat at tight end going into that game. The Jim Thorpe Award semifinalist said after the game that he was "just chillin'" and that he was dealing with "a little stinger." Bowen had been listed as "questionable" on previous availability reports this week. His brother, Eli was a late entry to the SEC availability report the day before the Texas game. He went through warmups prior to the game but was not available by kickoff. He has since missed the previous two games with an ankle injury. Pass catcher Elijah Thomas has missed the previous two weeks after sustaining an injury during the loss to Kentucky. He was downgraded as "out." Heath Ozaeta was taken off the report last weekend and after Thursday's report. He was technically available against Mississippi State but never played. home.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
home.blurb: Four Gators are listed as out: defensive lineman Jeramiah McCloud, tight end Evan Chieca, offensive lineman Emeka Ugorji and linebacker Jaden Robinson. McCloud is out due to a suspension, according to Swamp247 , while Robinson missed his first game of the season last week against Georgia. Listed as doubtful is wide receiver Vernell Brown III, who has missed the last four games with a grade-1 PCL strain that he suffered against Ole Miss in Week 4 that was re-aggravated ahead of last week's Georgia game. "So he was not available at practice today," Jon Sumrall said on Monday . "I really don't have a really strong feeling on timeline because everything early in the week last week was trending really positively until the setback on Wednesday. It sucks. It sucks for him. He's working like hell to try to get back. He's frustrated." The two players listed as questionable are wide receiver Bailey Stockton and defensive lineman Emmanuel Oyebadejo. Stockton has been dealing with a nagging foot injury but still played against the Bulldogs last week, finishing with 76 yards on eight catches. Wide receiver Elijah Thomas and offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis are listed as doubtful, while wide receiver Jer'Michael Carter, defensive backs Peyton Bowen and Eli Bowen, tight end Rocky Beers and defensive lineman Kenny Ozowalu are listed as questionable, and offensive lineman Jake Maikkula is listed as probable. "Jeramiah McCloud has been suspended for this week's game against Oklahoma for conduct detrimental to the team. His status with the program will be re-evaluated after this week's contest," per a statement from a program spokesperson. Sumrall added what he called his "official VB3 statement": "He wants to play. He's doing everything he can to play. He's pissed off he can't play, and he's doing everything in his power to play. It's a real injury that we thought we were on the other side of that he had a setback last week, and it sucks. I mean, it freaking sucks for him." Oklahoma has eight players who are not expected to play on Saturday: linebacker Taylor Heim, defensive back Dakoda Fields, wide receiver Trell Harris, linebacker Cole Sullivan, tight end Trynae Washington, defensive back Jacobe Johnson, and offensive linemen Ryan Fodje and Fred Hinton. home.headline: Florida's Eric Singleton returns to Atlanta still chasing Georgia win
home.blurb: Feeling great. Just trying to get back into tune with all my teammates and all the guys. Just ready to go out there and ball out Saturday. But seeing my guys still going out there and ball out brought my spirits up, and me getting back out there versus Ole Miss really showed me that I’m still able to help my team out. I just couldn’t keep watching my guys go out there having so much fun without me, man. I had to go out there and make a play. On whether anything would have kept him out against Ole Miss There are definitely some times where I’m hurting out there, but I still just push through it to try to help my team win. I’m confident in either one. Whoever comes out there Saturday, I just hope they’re ready to throw it. We talked about it during the week. I told him, in the game, I’m going to go get it, so let’s just put it out there. They’re very disciplined. I know Coach Kirby is probably on them very hard about being physical. You can see it on film. But I think we’re going to be able to go out there and out-physical them and play some hard-nosed football. Just how much of a man it made me become. The Atlanta youth football league out there, man, it’s very advanced. I was six when I started playing football. Where I’m from in Mississippi, they didn’t have a youth football league, so moving to Georgia, that was my first time ever seeing kids even play football for a team. It was a blessing to even be out there. Me personally, I think this is what I’m supposed to do. I can’t watch football. I hate just watching football. I have to be out there with my guys helping them. He takes some crazy hits out there. I don’t even know how he gets up myself. But he’s a dog, for sure. Eric Singleton Jr. has spent much of this season learning how to deal with something almost entirely unfamiliar to him: being injured. Singleton said this was the first significant injury of his football career, and watching from the sideline was nearly as mentally taxing as the physical recovery. He has pushed back onto the field despite still feeling some discomfort and believes he is getting close to full speed. Now he returns to Atlanta, where he grew up playing football, for another shot at a Georgia program he's already faced during his career. Singleton has yet to beat the Bulldogs or Kirby Smart, and he made no secret of wanting to change that this weekend. Here’s everything Singleton had to say ahead of Florida ’s matchup with Georgia. On dealing with the first injury of his career It was my first time ever being injured, so it was tough on me mentally at the beginning.
